Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 17, verse 1:

Explanation of the words:

Subhana (Glorified): i.e., He is exalted and sanctified above everything that does not befit His majesty and perfection, and He is Allah, may His majesty be exalted.

Bi-'abdihi (His servant): i.e., His servant and messenger Muhammad ﷺ.

Min al-Masjid al-Haram (from the Sacred Mosque): i.e., the one in Makkah.

Ila al-Masjid al-Aqsa (to the Furthest Mosque): i.e., the one in Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem).

Min ayatina (of Our signs): i.e., of the wonders of Our power and its manifestations in the Highest Kingdom.

Meaning of the noble verse:

The Lord, blessed and exalted, declared Himself free of what the polytheists attributed to Him of partners, daughters, and the attributes of created beings, and so He said: ﴿Glory be to Him who took His servant by night﴾, i.e., Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abd al-Muttalib ibn Hashim al-Qurashi al-Adnani, ﴿by night from the Sacred Mosque﴾, i.e., by night from the Sacred Mosque in Makkah, when he was taken out from the house of Umm Hani', his heart was washed with the water of Zamzam, and he was filled with faith and wisdom. Then he was taken by night from the Sacred Mosque to the Furthest Mosque, Bayt al-Maqdis. The Prophet ﷺ related that Allah gathered the prophets for him in the Furthest Mosque, and he led them in prayer as their imam, and thus he was the imam of the prophets and their seal. Then he was made to ascend to the heaven, heaven after heaven, finding in each heaven those brought near (to Allah), until he reached the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary (Sidrat al-Muntaha), near which is the Garden of Refuge (Jannat al-Ma'wa). Then he was made to ascend until he reached a level where he heard the scratching of the pens. As for the Most High's words ﴿the one whose surroundings We have blessed﴾, i.e., the surroundings of the Furthest Mosque; the meaning of "its surroundings" is the outward (blessing), which is by trees, rivers and fruits. As for its interior, the blessing is religious, through the multiplication of prayer within it, i.e., its reward, for a prayer there is worth five hundred prayers in reward and recompense. As for the Most High's words ﴿that We might show him of Our signs﴾, it is the reason for the night journey and the ascent, namely that He took His servant by night and made him ascend so that He might show him some of the wonders of His creation in the Highest Kingdom, and so that what he had learned by way of revelation he would know also by sight and witness. As for the Most High's words ﴿Indeed He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing﴾, He is describing Himself as the All-Hearing of His servants' words and the All-Seeing of their deeds and states. His wisdom required this wondrous night journey, so that those who believe may increase in faith, and that those who doubt may be in doubt and increase in disbelief and obstinacy.

Guidance from the noble verse:

Guidance from the noble verse:

1- Affirmation of the doctrine of the Night Journey and Ascension of the Prophet ﷺ, in both spirit and body together, from the Sacred Mosque to the Furthest Mosque, then to the highest heavens, up to a level where he heard the scratching of the pens, and Allah revealed to him what He revealed and enjoined upon him and his community the five daily prayers.

2- The excellence of the three mosques: the Sacred Mosque, the Mosque of the Prophet ﷺ, and the Furthest Mosque. The Sacred Mosque and the Furthest Mosque are mentioned explicitly in the text, while the Mosque of the Messenger ﷺ is mentioned by allusion and implication, since the word "Aqsa" (furthest) implies a "qusa" (far), and the "qasiy" (far one) is the Prophet's Mosque, while "al-Aqsa" is the mosque of Bayt al-Maqdis.

3- Explanation of the wisdom in the Night Journey and Ascension, which is that the Messenger ﷺ should see with his own eyes what he had believed in and learned by way of revelation, so that the unseen became witnessed to the Messenger of Allah.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 17, verses 2–6:

Explanation of the words:

"And We gave Musa the Book": that is, the Torah.

"And We made it guidance": that is, We made the Book, or Musa, a guidance, meaning a guide for the Children of Israel.

"A protector (wakil)": that is, a guardian, or a partner.

"Of those whom We carried": that is, in the ark.

"And We decreed": that is, We informed them of a decree that would reach them.

"In the Book": that is, the Torah.

"A great exaltation": that is, a tremendous transgression.

"The first of them": that is, the first of the two times.

"And they went through the habitations": that is, they moved back and forth, going and coming in the midst of the homes, killing and causing corruption.

"A promise fulfilled": that is, a promise carried out, which would not be broken.

Meaning of the verses:

He, exalted is He, informs that He is the One who took His servant by night from the Sacred Mosque to the Farthest Mosque, and that He is the One who gave Musa the Book, which is the Torah. So He, exalted is He, bestowed favour upon Muhammad (ﷺ) and upon his nation by the Night Journey (isra') and the Ascension (mi'raj), and upon Musa by giving him the Book so that it would be guidance and clarification for the Children of Israel. He is likewise bountiful toward the Children of Israel, so to Him belongs all praise and all grace.

His saying, "And We made it" (i.e., the Book) "guidance" means a clarification for the Children of Israel, by which they would be guided to the paths of perfection and felicity. His saying, "that you should not take besides Me a protector (wakil)" means: We gave Musa the Book and made it a guidance for the Children of Israel, so that they would not take other than Me as a guardian, associating him with Me by relying upon him and entrusting their affairs to him, forgetting Me while I am their Lord and the Bestower of their blessings. His exalted saying, "O offspring of those whom We carried with Nuh" means: O offspring of those whom We carried with Nuh, give thanks to Me as Nuh gave thanks to Me for delivering him in the ark along with his companions in it. "Indeed, he" (that is, Nuh) "was a grateful servant": so be like him, give thanks to Me by worshipping Me, make Me one, do not abandon My obedience, and do not associate anything with Me.

His exalted saying, "And We decreed to the Children of Israel in the Book that you will surely cause corruption in the land twice, and you will surely become exceedingly haughty" informs that He, exalted is He, made the Children of Israel aware of His decree concerning them, and that this was in their Book, the Torah: that they would cause corruption in the land by committing sins and falling into transgressions, and would become haughty in the land by daring against Allah and wronging the people, "a great exaltation," meaning a tremendous one. What He has decreed must certainly come to pass. His exalted saying, "So when the promise of the first of them came, We sent against you servants of Ours possessing great might," meaning strength and severe violence in war, came about when they corrupted and wronged by violating the bounds of the Shari'ah and turning away from obedience to Allah, to the extent that they killed their prophet Irmiya (Jeremiah), peace be upon him. This happened at the hand of the tyrant Jalut (Goliath), who invaded them from the land of al-Jazira, and did to them with his armies what Allah, exalted is He, described in His saying, "So they went through the habitations," going back and forth, killing, slaughtering, and corrupting: a retribution from Allah upon the Children of Israel for their corruption and their tremendous transgression.

His exalted saying, "And it was a promise fulfilled," means that what befell them in the first time of ruin and destruction, and its causes, was by a promise from Allah, exalted is He, which He carried out and fulfilled for them, because He had decreed it and informed them of it in their Book. His saying, "Then We gave you back the return over them," means: after many years, while the Children of Israel were oppressed and dispersed, a fresh generation arose among them and demanded that a king be appointed for them to lead them to jihad. This occurred as was mentioned in Surat al-Baqara: they fought, and Dawud (David) killed Jalut. This is the meaning of "Then We gave you back the return over them." His saying, "And We aided you with wealth and sons, and made you more numerous in manpower," means men for war; their wealth and children increased, and they established a state that ruled the world in the time of Dawud and Sulayman, peace be upon them.

Guidance from the verses:

1- A statement of Allah's bounty upon the Islamic and Israelite nations.

2- A statement of the purpose of the revelation of the books, which is to guide people to the worship of Allah and to His Oneness in it.

3- The obligation to give thanks to Allah for His blessings, since Nuh, peace be upon him, when he ate a meal would say "Praise be to Allah," when he drank would say "Praise be to Allah," when he put on his shoe would say "Praise be to Allah," and when he relieved a need would say "Praise be to Allah," and so he was named "a grateful servant." Likewise were the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the righteous of his nation until today.

4- What Allah has decreed will come to pass, and what He has promised will be fulfilled, and belief in this is obligatory.

5- Condemnation of corruption, wronging, and haughtiness in the land, and a statement of their evil consequence.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 17, verses 7–8:

Explanation of the words:

"If you do good": that is, obedience to Allah and His Messenger, performed sincerely and in the manner prescribed for it.

"You do good for yourselves": that is, the reward, recompense and good requital return to you, not to others.

"And if you do evil": that is, in obedience, then the evil consequence of the evil falls upon yourselves.

"The promise of the Hereafter": that is, the second time, corresponding to the first, which has already passed.

"To sadden your faces": that is, to disfigure them with distress and the blackness of grief, and they are humiliation.

"And to enter the Masjid": that is, Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem).

"And to destroy what they had conquered with complete destruction": that is, to destroy completely what they had overpowered of the lands of the Children of Israel.

"And if you return, We shall return": that is, if you return to corruption and sins, We shall return by empowering (others) over you.

"Hasiran" (a prison): that is, a confinement, a jail and a bed upon which they sit, so it is above them and beneath them.

Meaning of the verses:

The context continues speaking about the Children of Israel. After Allah informed them of what He had decreed against them in their Book, that they would cause corruption on the earth twice and would become exceedingly arrogant, and that when the time of the first of the two came He would send against them servants of great might, namely Goliath (Jalut) and his armies, who killed them and took them captive, Allah returned the turn to them, so they prevailed over them, David killed Goliath, and a great state was established for them, which was among the most populous states and the most extensive in authority. This was due to their return to Allah by applying His Book and adhering to His laws. There Allah said to them: "If you do good, you do good for yourselves," meaning: if you do good by following the truth and adhering to obedience to Allah and His Messenger, by performing what is commanded and avoiding what is forbidden, and by taking up the laws of Allah in human reform; and if you do evil, by neglecting the Sharia and immersing yourselves in pleasures and desires, the results of that return to yourselves according to the sunnah of Allah: "Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it, and will not find for himself, besides Allah, any protector or helper" [an-Nisa: 123]. His saying: "So when the promise of the Hereafter came" means its appointed time, which is the second time after the first. He also sent against them servants of His, namely Bukhtnasar (Nebuchadnezzar) and his armies, whom He sent against them to sadden their faces with what they inflicted on them of anxiety, grief, humiliation and abasement. "And that they might enter the Masjid" means Bayt al-Maqdis, as they had entered it the first time. "And that they might destroy what they had conquered" means: that they might destroy what they had overpowered of their lands, "with complete destruction," meaning total devastation and thorough demolition. This happened to them when they killed Zakariya and Yahya, peace be upon them, and many scholars, and after immorality had spread among them, and among their women there was display of adornment and lewdness, and the taking of high places. Thus the Messenger of Allah ﷺ informed of it.

His saying: "Perhaps your Lord will have mercy upon you" is a great good for them, which they would have attained had they sought it sincerely, but they turned away from it and lived in rebellion against the Sharia and disobedience to Allah and His messengers. His saying: "And if you return, We shall return" means: if you return to wickedness and immorality, We shall return by empowering whomever We will of Our servants. So Allah fulfilled what He had promised them: He empowered over them His Messenger Muhammad ﷺ and the believers, and he expelled the Banu Qaynuqa and the Banu al-Nadir from Madinah and killed the Banu Qurayza. Likewise there empowered over them the kings of Europe, who pursued them, inflicted upon them humiliation, and made them taste the evil of torment over long centuries. His saying: "And We have made Hell a prison for the disbelievers" means: if the torment of this world consists of being subjugated by oppressors, the stripping of their freedom, and the tasting of the torment of killing, captivity and dispersal, then the torment of the Hereafter is confinement and imprisonment in Hell, which will be a prison for the disbelievers, from which they will not come out. "The disbelievers" means those who reject the laws of Allah and His blessings upon them, by neglecting the rulings, squandering the obligations, neglecting the sunan, and immersing themselves in pleasures and desires.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of the verses:

1- The truthfulness of Allah's promise.

2- Confirmation of the prophethood of the Prophet ﷺ, since such reports are not related except by a prophet to whom revelation is sent.

3- Establishing the principle: "Whoever does righteousness, it is for his own self, and whoever does evil, it is against it" [Fussilat: 46; al-Jathiya: 15].

4- The obligation of hope in Allah, which is awaiting relief and good from Him, even if the time is long.

5- Allah may combine for the disbelievers the torment of this world and the torment of the Hereafter, and likewise for the sinful among the believers.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 17, verses 9–12:

Explanation of the words:

*Lil-lati hiya aqwam* (﴿لِلَّتِي هِيَ أَقْوَمُ﴾): That is, to the way that is most just and correct.

*Anna lahum ajran kabiran* (﴿أَنَّ لَهُمْ أَجْرًا كَبِيرًا﴾): It is Paradise, the Abode of Peace.

*A'tadna lahum 'adhaban alima* (﴿أَعْتَدْنَا لَهُمْ عَذَابًا أَلِيمًا﴾): It is the punishment of the Fire on the Day of Resurrection.

*Wa yad'u al-insanu bil-sharr* (﴿وَيَدْعُ الْإِنسَانُ بِالشَّرِّ﴾): That is, against himself and his family when he becomes impatient and angry.

*Wa kana al-insanu 'ajulan* (﴿وَكَانَ الْإِنسَانُ عَجُولًا﴾): That is, he is quick to be affected by whatever occurs to his mind, without deliberating or reflecting.

*Ayatayn* (﴿آيَتَيْنِ﴾): That is, two signs indicating the existence of God, His power, His knowledge, His mercy and His wisdom.

*Famahawna ayat al-layl* (﴿فَمَحَوْنَا آيَةَ اللَّيْلِ﴾): That is, We obliterated its light with the darkness that follows the setting of the sun.

*Mubsirah* (﴿مُبْصِرَةً﴾): That is, by which a person sees, by means of the daylight within it.

*Adad al-sinin wal-hisab* (﴿عَدَدَ السِّنِينَ وَالْحِسَابَ﴾): That is, the number of years, their passing, the beginning of their entry, and the reckoning of the hours of day and night and their times, such as days, weeks and months.

Meaning of the verses:

He, exalted is He, informs us that this Noble Qur'an, which He sent down to His servant and messenger Muhammad (ﷺ), who was taken on a night journey from the Sacred Mosque to the Farthest Mosque, guides by what it contains of proofs, arguments, laws and admonitions to the way and path that is most upright, that is, more just and more correct than all other ways and paths. It is the upright religion, Islam, the path of happiness and perfection in both abodes. ﴿And gives good news to the believers who do righteous deeds﴾: that is, the Qur'an gives good news to those who believed in God and His Messenger, in meeting God, and in His promise and His threat, and who did righteous deeds, which are the obligatory acts and the voluntary acts, after abstaining from major sins and transgressions, that for them is a great reward, namely Paradise. Likewise, it informs those who do not believe in the Hereafter that God has prepared for them a painful punishment in Hell.

His saying, exalted is He, ﴿And man prays for evil as he prays for good﴾: He, exalted is He, informs us about man in his weakness and his limited understanding of the consequences of matters, that when he becomes impatient or angry he prays against himself and his family for harm, without considering the consequence of his prayer were God to answer it. He prays for evil with the same eagerness with which he prays for good. His saying: ﴿And man has always been hasty﴾: that is, he is very hasty and rushes in all matters; this is his nature, unless he is disciplined by the manners of the Qur'an and adorns himself with its character. If he stays upright upon the method of the Qur'an, his nature is transformed and he becomes one of composure, forbearance, patience and deliberation.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We made the night and the day two signs﴾: that is, two signs of Our existence, Our power, Our knowledge and Our wisdom. His saying ﴿So We obliterated the sign of the night﴾: that is, by extinguishing its light. And We made the sign of the day to be illuminating, that is, shining. He explains the reason for this in His saying: ﴿that you may seek bounty from your Lord﴾: that is, that you may seek your provision through striving and earning during the day. This is one aspect; and on the other hand ﴿and that you may know the number of years and the reckoning﴾: that is, the number of years, their passing, the beginning of their entry, and the reckoning of the hours of day and night and their times, such as days, weeks and months, because your religious and worldly interests depend upon that. His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And every matter We have detailed with full detail﴾: that is, everything that man needs for his perfection and happiness We have made clear with clarification, namely in this Book which guides to that which is most upright.

Guidance from the verses:

1- Demonstration of the virtue of the Noble Qur'an, in its guidance to Islam, which is the path of happiness for man.

2- The promise and the threat: good news for the believers who do righteous deeds, and warning for the disbelievers in the Last Day.

3- Explanation of man's nature before he is refined by the Qur'anic manners and the prophetic character.

4- That the night and the day are two signs indicating God, the Exalted, and establishing His knowledge, power and governance.

5- The legitimacy of the science of calculation and learning it.

It is the upright religion, Islam, the path of happiness and perfection in both abodes. ﴿And gives good news to the believers who do righteous deeds﴾: that is, the Qur'an gives good news to those who believed in God and His Messenger, in meeting God, and in His promise and His threat, and who did righteous deeds, which are the obligatory acts and the voluntary acts, after abstaining from major sins and transgressions, that for them is a great reward, namely Paradise. Likewise, it informs those who do not believe in the Hereafter that God has prepared for them a painful punishment in Hell.

His saying, exalted is He, ﴿And man prays for evil as he prays for good﴾: He, exalted is He, informs us about man in his weakness and his limited understanding of the consequences of matters, that when he becomes impatient or angry he prays against himself and his family for harm, without considering the consequence of his prayer were God to answer it. He prays for evil with the same eagerness with which he prays for good. His saying: ﴿And man has always been hasty﴾: that is, he is very hasty and rushes in all matters; this is his nature, unless he is disciplined by the manners of the Qur'an and adorns himself with its character. If he stays upright upon the method of the Qur'an, his nature is transformed and he becomes one of composure, forbearance, patience and deliberation.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We made the night and the day two signs﴾: that is, two signs of Our existence, Our power, Our knowledge and Our wisdom. His saying ﴿So We obliterated the sign of the night﴾: that is, by extinguishing its light. And We made the sign of the day to be illuminating, that is, shining. He explains the reason for this in His saying: ﴿that you may seek bounty from your Lord﴾: that is, that you may seek your provision through striving and earning during the day. This is one aspect; and on the other hand ﴿and that you may know the number of years and the reckoning﴾: that is, the number of years, their passing, the beginning of their entry, and the reckoning of the hours of day and night and their times, such as days, weeks and months, because your religious and worldly interests depend upon that. His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And every matter We have detailed with full detail﴾: that is, everything that man needs for his perfection and happiness We have made clear with clarification, namely in this Book which guides to that which is most upright.

Guidance from the verses:

1- Demonstration of the virtue of the Noble Qur'an, in its guidance to Islam, which is the path of happiness for man.

2- The promise and the threat: good news for the believers who do righteous deeds, and warning for the disbelievers in the Last Day.

3- Explanation of man's nature before he is refined by the Qur'anic manners and the prophetic character.

4- That the night and the day are two signs indicating God, the Exalted, and establishing His knowledge, power and governance.

5- The legitimacy of the science of calculation and learning it.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 17, verses 13–17:

Explanation of the words:

Ta'irahu (ṭā'irahu): i.e., his deed and what was decreed for him of happiness and misery.

Fi 'unuqihi (fī ʿunuqihi): i.e., bound to him, never leaving him until it is finished.

ʿAlayka ḥasīban (ʿalayka ḥasīban): i.e., sufficient is your own self as a reckoner against you.

Wa-lā taziru wāziratun wizra ukhrā: i.e., no sinful soul shall bear the sin of another soul.

Mutrafīhā (mutrafīhā): its affluent ones, i.e., the pampered among its wealthy and its leaders.

Fa-ḥaqqa ʿalayhā al-qawl: i.e., the word (of punishment) became due against them.

Wa-kam ahlakanā (wa-kam ahlaknā): i.e., We destroyed many.

Min al-qurūn: i.e., of the people of the earlier generations.

Khabīran baṣīran: i.e., All-Knowing, All-Seeing of the sins of the servants.

Meaning of the verses:

He, the Exalted, informs that, by the greatness of His power, the breadth of His knowledge, and the wisdom of His governance, He has bound every person to what He has decreed for him of deeds, and to what follows from those deeds of happiness or misery in both abodes. He has bound him to this in such a way that he cannot oppose it or be delayed from it in any way, until it is as if it were tied around his neck. This is the meaning of His saying, ﴿And every person We have fastened his bird (deed) to his neck﴾. And His saying, ﴿And We will bring forth for him on the Day of Resurrection a record which he will find spread open﴾: that is, on the Day of Resurrection Allah, the Exalted, brings out for every person the record of his deeds, and he finds it spread open before him. It will be said to him: "Read your record; your own self suffices as a reckoner against you this day." That is, your self is sufficient as a reckoner of your deeds, counting them against you, O human. His saying, ﴿Whoever is guided is only guided for [the benefit of] his own soul, and whoever goes astray only strays to its detriment﴾: that is, after this announcement and clarification, one should know that whoever is guided today, believing in Allah and His Messenger, in meeting Allah, in His promise and His threat, and does righteous deeds, and abandons polytheism and sins, the benefit of that returns to him; he is the one who is saved from punishment and made happy in the abode of happiness. And whoever strays from the path of guidance, denying and not believing, associating partners with Allah and not monotheizing Him, and disobeying and not obeying, the harm of that straying returns upon him; he is the one who will be made miserable by it and punished in Hell, the abode of punishment and misery. His saying, ﴿And no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another﴾: "wizr" means sin and offense, and "wāziratun" is the one who carries it so as to be held accountable for it. The meaning is: on the Day of Resurrection no sinful soul will bear the sin of another soul; rather, each soul bears its own responsibility. The statement confirms His saying, ﴿Whoever is guided is only guided for [the benefit of] his own soul, and whoever goes astray only strays to its detriment.﴾ His saying, ﴿And We would never punish until We sent a messenger﴾: that is, it is not in the way of Allah, who is Just and Merciful, to destroy a nation with the punishment of annihilation and uprooting before sending among them a messenger who makes them know their Lord and what He loves and what He dislikes, and commands them to do what is good and to abandon what He dislikes, which is polytheism and sins. His saying, ﴿And when We intend to destroy a city﴾: that is, the people of a city, ﴿We command its affluent ones﴾: that is, We command its pampered ones among the wealthy, leaders, and nobles of those who loosen and bind, We command them to obey Us by establishing the Law and performing the obligations and recommended acts and avoiding major sins and grave immoralities. But they did not respond to the command or the prohibition; this is the meaning of ﴿so they committed sin therein, and the word became due against it﴾: that is, punishment became incumbent upon it. ﴿Then We destroyed it with complete destruction﴾: that is, We destroyed it utterly. This statement explains His saying, ﴿And We would never punish until We sent a messenger,﴾ since the messenger commands and forbids by the permission of Allah; if he is not obeyed, the people deserve punishment, and they are punished.

His saying, ﴿And how many generations have We destroyed after Noah﴾: this also confirms this ruling, since Allah, the Exalted, knows that what He reported was actually occurring. Many nations were destroyed by Him after the destruction of the people of Noah, such as ʿĀd, Thamūd, the people of Lot, the companions of the Thicket (al-Aykah), and the family of Pharaoh. His saying, ﴿And sufficient is your Lord as Knower and Seer of the sins of His servants﴾: although the statement includes Allah's knowledge of the sins of His servants, its meaning is a severe warning and a firm threat. He, the Exalted, does not approve of the continuation of crimes and sins; He gives respite so that people may perhaps awaken, so that the corrupt may perhaps refrain. Then, if they persist after being informed, and after their sins are denounced to them and their wrongdoing is made a cause of fear, He seizes them with the seizure of the Mighty, the Omnipotent. Let those who persist in polytheism and sins beware of that!

Guidance from the verses:

1- Affirmation of the doctrine of qadar (divine decree).

2- Affirmation of the doctrine of resurrection and recompense.

3- Affirmation of divine justice on the Day of Resurrection, so that no soul is wronged in anything.

4- Explanation of Allah's way regarding the destruction of nations, that they are not destroyed except after warning and giving them notice.

5- Warning against excessive luxury and affluence, for it leads to corruption through abandoning obedience, and corruption then leads to destruction and ruin.

His saying, ﴿And no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another﴾: "wizr" means sin and offense, and "wāziratun" is the one who carries it so as to be held accountable for it. The meaning is: on the Day of Resurrection no sinful soul will bear the sin of another soul; rather, each soul bears its own responsibility. The statement confirms His saying, ﴿Whoever is guided is only guided for [the benefit of] his own soul, and whoever goes astray only strays to its detriment.﴾ His saying, ﴿And We would never punish until We sent a messenger﴾: that is, it is not in the way of Allah, who is Just and Merciful, to destroy a nation with the punishment of annihilation and uprooting before sending among them a messenger who makes them know their Lord and what He loves and what He dislikes, and commands them to do what is good and to abandon what He dislikes, which is polytheism and sins. His saying, ﴿And when We intend to destroy a city﴾: that is, the people of a city, ﴿We command its affluent ones﴾: that is, We command its pampered ones among the wealthy, leaders, and nobles of those who loosen and bind, We command them to obey Us by establishing the Law and performing the obligations and recommended acts and avoiding major sins and grave immoralities. But they did not respond to the command or the prohibition; this is the meaning of ﴿so they committed sin therein, and the word became due against it﴾: that is, punishment became incumbent upon it. ﴿Then We destroyed it with complete destruction﴾: that is, We destroyed it utterly. This statement explains His saying, ﴿And We would never punish until We sent a messenger,﴾ since the messenger commands and forbids by the permission of Allah; if he is not obeyed, the people deserve punishment, and they are punished.

His saying, ﴿And sufficient is your Lord as Knower and Seer of the sins of His servants﴾: although the statement includes Allah's knowledge of the sins of His servants, its meaning is a severe warning and a firm threat. He, the Exalted, does not approve of the continuation of crimes and sins; He gives respite so that people may perhaps awaken, so that the corrupt may perhaps refrain. Guidance from the verses:

1- Affirmation of the doctrine of qadar (divine decree).

2- Affirmation of the doctrine of resurrection and recompense.

3- Affirmation of divine justice on the Day of Resurrection, so that no soul is wronged in anything.

4- Explanation of Allah's way regarding the destruction of nations, that they are not destroyed except after warning and giving them notice.

5- Warning against excessive luxury and affluence, for it leads to corruption through abandoning obedience, and corruption then leads to destruction and ruin.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 17, verse 18–22:

Explanation of the words:

Al-'ajilah (the hastening one): that is, the worldly life, because of how quickly it passes away.

Yaslaha madhmuman madhduran (he will burn in it, blamed and cast out): that is, he will enter it, blameworthy and removed far from Paradise.

Wa sa'a laha sa'yaha (and strives for it with the striving due to it): that is, he does for it the work required for entering it, which is faith and righteous deeds.

Kana sa'yuhum mashkuran (their striving was appreciated): that is, their deed was accepted and rewarded by Allah the Exalted.

Kullan numiddu ha'ulaa'i wa ha'ulaa' (to each We extend, these and those): that is, to each of the two groups We give.

Wa ma kana 'ata'u rabbika mahzuran (and the gift of your Lord was not restricted): that is, the gift of Allah in this world was not restricted, meaning not withheld from anyone.

Kayfa faddalna ba'dahum 'ala ba'd (how We have favoured some of them over others): that is, in provision and standing.

La taj'al ma'a Allahi ilahan akhar (do not set up with Allah another god): that is, do not worship with Allah the Exalted anything else among all the false objects of worship.

Fa taq'uda maluman makhdhulan (so you will sit blamed and forsaken): that is, you will become blamed by the angels and the believers, and forsaken by Allah the Exalted.

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues with the true reports of Allah the Exalted, which contain various kinds of divine guidance that none is deprived of except one who is destroyed. Allah the Exalted says in the noble verse [18] ﴿Whoever desires the hastening one (the worldly life)﴾, that is, the world, ﴿We hasten for him therein what We will, for whom We intend﴾, not what the servant wills; and His saying ﴿for whom We intend﴾ means not for whomever else wills, for the whole matter belongs to Us. ﴿Then﴾ after that ﴿We have made for him Hell, he will burn in it, blamed and cast out﴾, that is, blameworthy, ﴿removed far away﴾, that is, expelled from Our mercy, which is Paradise, the abode of the righteous, that is, the obedient and sincere. And His saying in the second verse [19] ﴿And whoever desires the Hereafter﴾ informs that whoever desires the Hereafter, that is, the happiness of the Hereafter, ﴿and strives for it with the striving due to it﴾, that is, does for it the deed fitting for it, which is sound faith and righteous deeds conforming to what Allah prescribed in His Book and upon the tongue of His Messenger, and avoids shirk and sins; and His saying ﴿while he is a believer﴾ is a condition for the validity of the righteous deed, that is, no prayer or struggle is accepted from a servant except after his faith in Allah, in His Messenger, and in everything His Messenger brought and reported of the unseen.

And His saying ﴿those﴾, that is, those mentioned with faith and righteous deeds, ﴿their striving was appreciated﴾, that is, their deed was accepted, and they will be rewarded for it with Paradise and the pleasure of Allah the Exalted. And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿To each of these and those We extend from the gift of your Lord, and the gift of your Lord is not restricted﴾, that is, each of the seekers of the world and the seekers of the Hereafter, Allah extends to these and those from His gift, that is, His vast bounty; all eat, drink and clothe themselves according to what is decreed for them of constraint and abundance, then they die, and the difference arises according to corrupt or righteous striving. And His saying ﴿and the gift of your Lord is not restricted﴾ means that whoever Allah wishes to give something, no one can divert it from him or withhold it from him in any circumstance. And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Look how We have favoured some of them over others﴾, that is, look, O our Messenger, and whoever understands Our address, how We have favoured some people over others in provision, which includes health, well-being, wealth, offspring and standing. When you know this, then know that the Hereafter is greater in degrees and greater in favour, and that is returned to the bounty of Allah first, then to acquisition, in righteousness and corruption, abundance and scarcity, as is also the case in this world; according to a person's righteous acquisition for this world he obtains it, even if he is a disbeliever, by His saying in Surah Hud ﴿Whoever desires the life of this world and its adornment, We will pay them in full for their deeds therein, and they therein will not be deprived﴾ [Hud: 15], that is, their deeds' fruits are not diminished because they are disbelievers and polytheists.

And His saying: ﴿Do not set up with Allah another god﴾, that is, do not set up, O our Messenger, with Allah another god that you believe in, worship, and affirm his divinity apart from Us; for if you did so — and far be it from him to do so, since Allah does not want that for him — ﴿you will sit blamed and forsaken﴾, that is, blamed by the believers and the angels, forsaken by your Lord with no helper for you. Although the context addresses the Messenger ﷺ, the intended meaning is every human being: Allah forbids His servant to worship anything alongside Him, and misery follows from that, we seek refuge in Allah the Exalted.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of the verses:

1- In both abodes, happiness or misery depends on acquisition and action; this is the sunnah of Allah the Exalted regarding His servants.

2- The striving of this world is trade, farming and industry.

3- The striving of the Hereafter is faith, righteous deeds, and freeing oneself from shirk and sins.

4- Allah the Exalted gives worldly provision to whom He loves and to whom He does not love, and His giving is based on laws He has set in life which must be known and acted upon by whoever desires both this world and the Hereafter.

5- What Allah gives, no one can withhold; therefore it is obligatory to rely upon Allah and turn away from all else.

6- The prohibition of shirk and the threat of eternal abiding in the Fire of Hell for it.

And His saying ﴿those﴾, that is, those mentioned with faith and righteous deeds, ﴿their striving was appreciated﴾, that is, their deed was accepted, and they will be rewarded for it with Paradise and the pleasure of Allah the Exalted. And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿To each of these and those We extend from the gift of your Lord, and the gift of your Lord is not restricted﴾, that is, each of the seekers of the world and the seekers of the Hereafter, Allah extends to these and those from His gift, that is, His vast bounty; all eat, drink and clothe themselves according to what is decreed for them of constraint and abundance, then they die, and the difference arises according to corrupt or righteous striving. And His saying ﴿and the gift of your Lord is not restricted﴾ means that whoever Allah wishes to give something, no one can divert it from him or withhold it from him in any circumstance. And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Look how We have favoured some of them over others﴾, that is, look, O our Messenger, and whoever understands Our address, how We have favoured some people over others in provision, which includes health, well-being, wealth, offspring and standing. When you know this, then know that the Hereafter is greater in degrees and greater in favour, and that is returned to the bounty of Allah first, then to acquisition, in righteousness and corruption, abundance and scarcity, as is also the case in this world; according to a person's righteous acquisition for this world he obtains it, even if he is a disbeliever, by His saying in Surah Hud ﴿Whoever desires the life of this world and its adornment, We will pay them in full for their deeds therein, and they therein will not be deprived﴾ [Hud: 15], that is, their deeds' fruits are not diminished because they are disbelievers and polytheists.

And His saying: ﴿Do not set up with Allah another god﴾, that is, do not set up, O our Messenger, with Allah another god that you believe in, worship, and affirm his divinity apart from Us; for if you did so — and far be it from him to do so, since Allah does not want that for him — ﴿you will sit blamed and forsaken﴾, that is, blamed by the believers and the angels, forsaken by your Lord with no helper for you. Although the context addresses the Messenger ﷺ, the intended meaning is every human being: Allah forbids His servant to worship anything alongside Him, and misery follows from that, we seek refuge in Allah the Exalted.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of the verses:

1- In both abodes, happiness or misery depends on acquisition and action; this is the sunnah of Allah the Exalted regarding His servants.

2- The striving of this world is trade, farming and industry.

3- The striving of the Hereafter is faith, righteous deeds, and freeing oneself from shirk and sins.

4- Allah the Exalted gives worldly provision to whom He loves and to whom He does not love, and His giving is based on laws He has set in life which must be known and acted upon by whoever desires both this world and the Hereafter.

5- What Allah gives, no one can withhold; therefore it is obligatory to rely upon Allah and turn away from all else.

6- The prohibition of shirk and the threat of eternal abiding in the Fire of Hell for it.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 17, verses 23–27:

Explanation of the words:

"And your Lord has decreed" (Wa qada rabbuka): means commanded and enjoined.

"And to parents, good treatment" (Wa bil-walidayni ihsanan): means and that you should treat your parents well, and that is by being dutiful to them.

"Do not say to them, 'Uff'" (Fa la taqul lahuma uff): means cursed be, or ugliness, or loss.

"And do not scold them" (Wa la tanharhuma): means do not rebuke them with harsh words.

"A gracious word" (Qawlan karIman): means beautiful and gentle.

"The wing of humility" (Janah al-dhull): means lower to them your side and be humble toward them.

"For those who turn back" (Kana lil-awwabin): means those who return to obedience after disobedience.

"And give to the near of kin" (Wa ati dhal-qurba): means give those who have ties of kinship their rights of goodness and kindness.

"And do not squander wastefully" (Wa la tubadhdhir tabdhira): means do not spend wealth in what is not obedience to Allah and His Messenger.

"Ungrateful to his Lord" (Li-rabbihi kafura): means greatly ungrateful to the blessings of his Lord, the Exalted; and likewise the squanderer is his brother.

Meaning of the verses:

When Allah, the Exalted, forbade shirk and His Messenger was forbidden it by His saying, "Do not set up with Allah another god, lest you sit reproached and forsaken" [al-Isra': 17], He commanded tawhid, saying: "And your Lord has decreed" (Wa qada rabbuka), meaning He judged, commanded and enjoined, "that you not worship except Him" (alla ta'budu illa iyyah), meaning that you should not worship anyone except Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. His saying, the Exalted: "And to parents, good treatment" (Wa bil-walidayni ihsanan), meaning and He enjoined good treatment toward the parents, the mother and the father, which is being dutiful to them, by bringing good to them, withholding harm from them, and obeying them in what does not involve disobedience to Allah, the Exalted. His saying, the Exalted: "If one or both of them reach old age with you, do not say to them, 'Uff,' and do not scold them" (Imma yablughanna 'indaka al-kibar ahaduhuma aw kilahuma fa la taqul lahuma uff wa la tanharhuma), meaning: if one of them, the father or the mother, or both of them, reach old age while you are alive and present with them in this state, it is obligatory that you serve them as they served you when you were a child: you wash their urine and cleanse their filth, and provide what they need, and you do not feel impatient or say "uff" at serving them, just as they used to do for you when you were a child who urinated and defecated while they washed and cleaned you and did not feel impatient or say "uff." His saying: "And do not scold them" (Wa la tanharhuma), meaning do not rebuke them with a loud, offensive word. "And speak to them a gracious word" (Wa qul lahuma qawlan karIman), meaning a beautiful, easy, gentle word, with which they feel honor and respect. His saying, the Exalted: "And lower to them the wing of humility out of mercy" (Wa-khfid lahuma janah al-dhull min al-rahmah), meaning be gentle with them, humble yourself, show them compassion and mercy. Pray for them throughout your life for forgiveness and mercy if they were monotheists and died in that state, because of His saying, the Exalted: "It is not for the Prophet and those who believe to ask forgiveness for the polytheists, even if they were relatives" [al-Tawbah: 113], and this is the meaning of His saying, the Exalted: "And say, 'My Lord, have mercy on them as they brought me up when I was small'" (Wa qul rabbi-rhamhuma kama rabbayani saghIran). His saying, the Exalted: "Your Lord is most knowing of what is in your souls; if you are righteous, then indeed He is ever forgiving to those who turn back" (Rabbukum a'lamu bima fi nufusikum in takunu salihin fa-innahu kana lil-awwabina ghafura).

He, the Exalted, informs that He knows us better than we know ourselves. Whoever harbors in his heart dissatisfaction with his parents and anger toward them, Allah knows it of him, and whoever harbors love for them, respect for them, and contentment with them and from them, Allah, the Exalted, knows it and will recompense him for it. The one who does good is repaid with good, and the one who does evil is repaid with evil. His saying: "If you are righteous, then indeed He is ever forgiving to those who turn back" (in takunu salihin fa-innahu kana lil-awwabina ghafura) is in accordance with human weakness, for a person may at times harbor evil toward his parents, or a bad impulse may escape him in word or deed, while he is otherwise righteous, fulfilling the rights of Allah, the rights of his parents, and the rights of people. This righteous servant is informed by Allah, the Exalted, that He is forgiving to him whenever he returns to Allah, the Exalted, seeking forgiveness for what proceeded from him, and regretful of it.

His saying, the Exalted: "And give the near of kin his due, and the needy and the wayfarer" (Wa ati dha al-qurba haqqahu wal-miskina wabn al-sabil). This is Allah's command to the believing servant to give his relatives their rights of goodness and kinship, and likewise the needy (al-masakin), who are the poor whom destitution has rendered helpless and whom poverty has humbled. Allah, the Exalted, commands the believer to give these their rights through kindness to them by clothing, food, and a good word. Likewise the wayfarer (ibn al-sabil), who is the traveler: his due is to be given hospitality and help with his journey if he needs it, along with protection and guidance to his route. His saying, the Exalted: "And do not squander wastefully" (Wa la tubadhdhir tabdhira), meaning do not spend your wealth or scatter it in what is not obedience to Allah, the Exalted. His saying: "Indeed, the squanderers are brothers of the devils" (Inna al-mubadhdhirina kanu ikhwan al-shayatin), because by squandering their wealth in acts of disobedience they became rebels against Allah, defiant of His command, and this is the condition of the devils, so they resembled one another and became brothers. His saying: "And Satan was ever ungrateful to his Lord" (wa kana al-shaytanu li-rabbihi kafura), because he disobeyed Allah, the Exalted, and denied His blessings upon him, and did not thank Him by obeying Him. The squanderer of wealth in sins has transgressed the command of his Lord and not thanked His blessings upon him, so he is, in that case, a devil. Would a Muslim servant of Allah be pleased to be a devil?

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of the verses:

1- The obligation to worship Allah alone, and the obligation to be dutiful to parents, which is treating them well, withholding harm from them, and obeying them in what is right.

2- The obligation to supplicate for one's parents for forgiveness and mercy.

3- The obligation to be mindful of Allah, the Exalted, and not to harbor any evil in the soul.

4- Whoever is righteous and a bad impulse escapes him, then repents from it, Allah will forgive him for it.

5- The obligation to give the near of kin their rights of goodness and kinship, and likewise the needy and the wayfarer.

6- The prohibition of squandering, and its reality is spending wealth on sins and forbidden things.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 17, verses 28–33:

Explanation of the words:

﴿And if you turn away from them﴾: that is, from those mentioned: the near of kin, the needy, and the wayfarer, so that you give them nothing.

﴿Seeking mercy from your Lord which you hope for﴾: that is, seeking provision which you hope for from Allah, the Exalted.

﴿A gentle word﴾: that is, soft and easy speech, by promising them a gift when provision is available.

﴿Your hand chained to your neck﴾: that is, do not withhold expenditure, as if your hand were tied to your neck so that you cannot give anything.

﴿Nor extend it fully outstretched﴾: that is, do not spend everything in your hand so that you leave nothing behind.

﴿So you sit reproached﴾: that is, reproached by those whom you deprived of spending.

﴿Destitute﴾: that is, cut off from your journey through life, since you have left yourself with nothing.

﴿Extends provision and restricts it﴾: that is, He widens it, and restricts it, as a trial and a test.

﴿For fear of poverty﴾: that is, the fear of poverty and its severity.

﴿A great sin﴾: that is, a grave offence.

﴿An abomination and an evil way﴾: that is, a vile deed of extreme vileness; and "an evil way" means how wretched the way is.

﴿Authority﴾: that is, to his heir, a power over the killer.

﴿Let him not commit excess in killing﴾: that is, let him not kill other than the killer.

The meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues with the precepts of the Lord, blessed and exalted, which are rulings revealed by Allah, the Exalted, to His Messenger, so that they may be followed for guidance, perfection, and happiness. As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And if you turn away from them, seeking mercy from your Lord which you hope for, then speak to them a gentle word﴾: that is, if you turn away from your kin, or from a needy person who asked you, or a wayfarer who needed you, and you find nothing to give them, and so you turn your face away from them, O Messenger, ﴿then speak to them a gentle word﴾: that is, soft and easy speech, which is a good promise, such as your saying, "If Allah grants me provision, I will give you," or "Soon something will come to me and I will give you such-and-such," and similar good promises. That will be a gift from you to them in the present, by which they are gladdened and do not grieve. As for His saying: ﴿And do not make your hand chained to your neck﴾: that is, do not be stingy with what Allah has given you, so that you deprive those with rights of their rights, as if your hand were fastened to your neck so that you cannot spend. As for His saying: ﴿Nor extend it fully outstretched﴾: that is, do not open your hands in giving so that you bring out everything in your pocket or your treasury and leave nothing for yourself or your family. As for His saying: ﴿So you sit reproached and destitute﴾: that is, if you withhold and do not spend, your askers will blame you for not giving them; and if you spend everything you have, life will cut you off and you will not find what you need to continue your journey through the rest of your life. You will be like the camel whose exertion has worn it out, so it is left behind on the road, exhausted, and its owner cannot bring it back to his family nor continue the journey on it to his destination. As for His saying: ﴿Indeed, your Lord extends provision for whom He wills﴾: that is, He widens it for whom He wills, as a test of whether he will be grateful or ungrateful, and He restricts it for whom He wills, that is, He narrows it for whom He wills, as a trial of whether he will be patient or impatient and angry. ﴿Indeed He is ever, of His servants, Acquainted and Seeing﴾: so He widens and restricts according to His knowledge and wisdom, for among His servants there is one whom only abundance suits, and among them one whom only restriction suits. As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And do not kill your children for fear of poverty﴾: that is, and among what He has decreed and enjoined: ﴿And do not kill your children﴾: that is, your offspring ﴿for fear of poverty﴾: that is, apprehension of destitution and want, since the Arabs used to bury daughters alive for fear of shame, and killed their sons as well as daughters for fear of destitution. So Allah, the Exalted, enjoined the prohibition of that, and, as a guarantor who takes responsibility for the provision of the children and their fathers, said: ﴿We provide for them and for you.﴾ He, the Exalted, informed that killing children ﴿is ever a great sin﴾: that is, a grave offence. How then could a believer commit it?

As for His saying: ﴿And do not approach fornication; indeed, it is ever an abomination and an evil way﴾: that is, among what He has decreed and enjoined is that you, O believers, not even approach fornication, merely drawing near to it before committing it, because fornication, by Allah's ruling, is an abomination, that is, a vile deed of extreme vileness, abhorred by nature, reason, and the Sharia; and "an evil way" means the path leading to fornication is wretched, given the evil effects and destructive results that follow from it, the first of which is harming believers in their honour, and the last of which is Hell, burning in its fire and remaining in it for long ages. As for His saying: ﴿And do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden, except by right﴾: that is, among what Allah, the Exalted, has decreed and enjoined is that you, O believers, not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden to be killed, except by right. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) explained the right by which a believer's soul may be taken, which is one of three: deliberate killing with aggression, adultery after marriage (ihsan), and apostasy after faith. As for His saying: ﴿And whoever is killed wrongfully, We have given his heir authority﴾: that is, whoever has a slain relative killed unjustly and aggressively, that is, not by error, Allah, the Exalted, has given his heir complete authority over the killer: if he wills, he may kill him; if he wills, he may take blood-money from him; and if he wills, he may pardon him for the sake of Allah, the Exalted. And as for His saying: ﴿So let him not commit excess in killing; indeed, he is ever supported﴾: that is, it is not lawful for the heir of the blood, that is, the one whose slain relative was killed, to commit excess in killing, by killing more than one in place of one, or killing a man in place of a woman, or killing other than the killer. That is because Allah, the Exalted, has given him an authority that enables him to kill his killer, so it is not permissible for him to kill other than his killer, as they used to do in the Jahiliyyah.

Guidance from the verses:

1- A good word stands in place of charity for one who has nothing to give to the one who asks.

2- The prohibition of both stinginess and extravagance, and the virtue of moderation and balance.

3- The manifestation of Allah's wisdom in widening provision for some people and restricting it for others.

4- The prohibition of killing children after birth, or aborting them before birth, for fear of poverty or shame.

5- The prohibition of the preliminaries to fornication, such as looking with desire, speaking with a non-related person, and touching her, and the prohibition of fornication itself, which is graver.

6- The prohibition of killing a soul which Allah has forbidden to be killed, except by right; and the right is deliberate killing with aggression, adultery after marriage, and apostasy after faith.

**Explanation of the Words:**

**إلا بالتي هي أحسن** (*illa bi-llati hiya ahsan*): That is, except by the way that is better than others, which is to develop it and to spend from it on him in a fair manner.

**حتى يبلغ أشده** (*hatta yablugha ashuddahu*): That is, until he reaches the age of responsibility while being sound of mind and mature in judgment.

**وأوفوا بالعهد** (*wa-awfu bil-ahd*): That is, if you make a covenant with God or with people, then fulfill what you have covenanted.

**إن العهد كان مسئولا** (*inna al-ahda kana mas'ula*): That is, about it. The servant will be asked on the Day of Resurrection: "Why did you break your covenant?"

**أوفوا الكيل** (*awfu al-kayl*): That is, complete it and do not diminish it.

**بالقسطاس المستقيم** (*bil-qistas al-mustaqim*): That is, the balanced and upright scale.

**وأحسن تأويلا** (*wa-ahsanu ta'wila*): That is, better in outcome and consequence.

**ولا تقف** (*wa la taqfu*): That is, and do not follow.

**والفؤاد** (*wal-fu'ad*): That is, the heart.

**كان عنه مسئولا** (*kana 'anhu mas'ula*): That is, each of these three senses will be questioned about on the Day of Resurrection.

**مرحا** (*maraḥan*): That is, with arrogance and conceit.

**لن تخرق الأرض** (*lan takhriqa al-arda*): That is, you will not pierce or split the earth with your feet.

**من الحكمة** (*min al-hikma*): That is, wisdom, which is knowing what is beloved to God, in order to draw near to Him through it, and knowing what displeases Him, in order to avoid it, drawing near to Him by that.

**ملوما مدحورا** (*mal'uman madhuran*): That is, you will blame yourself for your association of partners with your Lord, being cast away from the mercy of God.

**Explanation of the Meanings of the Verses:**

The noble context continues to explain what God has decreed for His believing servants and has enjoined upon them. He says, ﴿And do not approach the property of the orphan﴾, that is, O believers, ﴿except in the way that is best﴾, that is, in the manner that is most excellent. This means that you deal with it by making it grow and by managing it well, and by spending from it upon the orphan in a fair manner. As for consuming it extravagantly and hastily, that is forbidden. His saying, ﴿until he reaches maturity﴾, means until he reaches the age of right judgment, then you hold him accountable and give him his property to dispose of according to what is permitted of financial dealings. His saying, may He be exalted, ﴿And fulfill the covenant﴾, means: and among what He has enjoined upon you is that you fulfill your covenants, both those between you and your Lord and those between you and all other people, whether believers or disbelievers. Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 17, verses 40–44:

Explanation of the words:

*Afa-asfakum* (أفأصفاكم): The interrogative is for reproach and rebuke. *Asfakum* means He singled you out for sons and chose them for you.

*Wa-laqad sarrafna fi hadha al-Qur'an* (ولقد صرفنا في هذا القرآن): That is, We made clear in it the promise and the threat, the parables, the admonitions, the rulings and the lessons.

*Li-yadhdhakkaru* (ليذكروا): That is, so that they may be mindful, be admonished, believe and obey.

*La-ibtaghaw ila dhi al-'arsh sabilan* (لابتغوا إلى ذي العرش سبيلا): That is, they would have sought a way to God, the Exalted, to draw near to Him and to seek a station with Him.

*Wa-man fihinna* (ومن فيهن): That is, in the heavens, the angels, and on the earth, humans, jinn and animals.

*Wa-in min shay'in illa yusabbihu* (وإن من شيء إلا يسبح): That is, there is nothing among all created things that does not glorify Him with His praise.

*Haliman ghafuran* (حليماً غفوراً): In that He did not hasten to punish you for your disobedience to Him and your failure to obey Him.

Meaning of the verses:

He, the Exalted, rebukes and reproaches the polytheists who buried their daughters and hated them, yet attribute angels as females: ﴿Has your Lord then singled you out for sons and taken for Himself daughters from among the angels? Indeed, you utter a monstrous saying.﴾ That is, He singled you out for sons, O polytheists, when you ascribe to God what you hate, a fabrication and a lie against God, the Exalted. His saying: ﴿And We have certainly diversified in this Qur'an⦆ means: among the proofs, clear evidences, parables and admonitions, a great deal, so that they may be mindful, be admonished, and turn to their Lord, believing in His oneness and exalting Him above partners and offspring. But the Qur'an and what it contains of clear proofs and guidance only increase them in aversion and distance from the truth. This is due to their dominant blind imitation, obstinacy, arrogance and denial. His saying: ﴿Say: If there were gods with Him, as they say⦆ means: Say, O our Prophet, to these polytheists who set up rivals to God and claim they are gods with God: if there were gods with God as you say, and although reality refutes you, since there are no gods with God, but supposing there were gods with God, ﴿they would surely have sought a way to the Lord of the Throne⦆, that is, they would have sought a path to the Lord of the Throne, glorified and exalted, seeking His pleasure and striving to draw near to Him and to be brought close to Him, because of His majesty and perfection, His self-sufficiency and their need and dependence upon Him. Then He, glorified and exalted, declared Himself free of having any gods with Him, saying: ﴿Glory be to Him, and exalted far above what they say, with a great exaltation.﴾ His saying: ﴿The seven heavens and the earth and whatever is in them glorify Him⦆: He, the Exalted, declared Himself free, sanctifying His essence above likeness, partner, offspring and incapacity. He informed that, due to His greatness and perfection, the seven heavens, the earth and whatever is in them glorify Him with the words: "Glory be to God and praise be to Him." ﴿And there is not a thing but glorifies His praise⦆, as He informed that there is no created thing that does not glorify Him with His praise, with the tongue of its speech and its state together, saying: "Glory be to God and praise be to Him." His saying: ﴿But you do not understand their glorification⦆ is due to the difference of tongues and languages. His saying, "if He is" (that is, God): ﴿Forbearing⦆: He does not hasten to punish whoever disobeys Him; ﴿Forgiving⦆: He forgives the sins and lapses of whoever repents to Him, turns to Him in penitence, seeking His forgiveness and pleasure.

Guidance of the verses

From the guidance of these verses:

1- The prohibition of speaking about God falsely and of attributing deficiency to Him, such as ascribing to Him a son or a partner.

2- The legitimacy of reasoning from rational proofs to establish truth and refute falsehood.

3- The virtue of glorification, which is the saying "Glory be to God and praise be to Him," so that whoever says it a hundred times, his sins are forgiven, even if they are as numerous as the foam of the sea.

4- All creatures in all worlds glorify God, the Exalted, that is, they declare Him free of partners, offspring, deficiency, incapacity and resemblance to created things, for "there is nothing like unto Him, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing."

5- God's forbearance is manifest in not hastening the punishment of those who disobey Him. Were it not for His forbearance, He would have hastened the punishment of the polytheists of Makkah and its chief criminals. But God gave them respite until most of them repented.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 17, verses 45–48:

Explanation of the words:

*Hijaban mastura* (a concealing veil): that is, a covering that conceals, so they do not hear the speech of God Most High.

*Wa ja'alna 'ala qulubihim akinna* (And We have placed over their hearts coverings): that is, coverings over the hearts, so that they neither comprehend nor understand.

*Wa fi adhanihim waqra* (And in their ears a deafness): that is, a heaviness, so that they do not hear the Qur'an and its admonitions.

*Wa law 'ala adbarihim nufura* (And if they turn their backs in aversion): that is, fleeing from hearing, so that they do not listen.

*Bima yastami'una bihi* (With what they listen to it): that is, because of it, namely mocking the Prophet ﷺ.

*Wa idh hum najwa* (And when they hold secret counsel): that is, they confer privately among themselves, speaking in secret.

*Rajulan maskhura* (a man bewitched): that is, one whose mind has been overpowered and deceived.

*Darabu laka al-amthal* (They have struck for you the parables): that is, they said "a sorcerer," they said "a soothsayer," and they said "a poet."

*Fa dallu* (So they have gone astray): that is, from guidance, so they cannot find a way.

Meaning of the verses:

God Most High says: *"And when you recite the Qur'an"*, informing His Messenger Muhammad ﷺ that when he recites the Qur'an to the polytheists in order to call them through it to God Most High, that they may believe in it and worship Him alone, God Most High places between him and the polytheists a concealing veil, or a hidden barrier, which cannot be seen. It truly is a barrier between them and the Messenger ﷺ, so that they do not hear the Qur'an that is recited to them and so gain no benefit from it. This veil results from the intensity of their hatred for the Messenger ﷺ and their aversion to his call, so they neither see him nor hear his recitation. His words: *"And We have placed over their hearts coverings lest they should comprehend it"*: *akinna* is the plural of *kinan*, which is a covering, so that the meaning recited from the verses does not reach their hearts and they do not comprehend it. His words: *"And in their ears a deafness"*: that is, God Most High placed in the ears of those opposing polytheists a heaviness, so that they do not hear the Qur'an that is recited to them. All of this is part of the concealing veil and the coverings. The deafness in the ears is a punishment from God Most High upon them, by which He deprived them of guidance through the Qur'an, because of the evil that preceded in them. God did not wrong them, but they were the wrongdoers, through their hatred of the Messenger and what he brought, and their hostility toward him and toward the monotheism and the true religion that he carried. His words: *"And when you mention your Lord in the Qur'an, alone"*: by saying "There is no god but God," or by making clear the meaning of "There is no god but God," the polytheists turned away in aversion, fleeing from hearing monotheism, because of their love for idolatry and their hearts' attachment to shirk.

His words: *"We know best what they listen to when they listen to you"*: God Most High says to His Messenger: We know best what the polytheists listen for, that is, that they listen in order to mock you and ridicule you and what you recite, not that they listen for knowledge and understanding, or to seek the truth and be guided to it. His words: *"When they listen to you, and when they are in secret counsel"*: that is, some of them confer with one another, *"when the wrongdoers say"*: that is, the polytheists, *"You follow only a man bewitched"*: that is, one deceived and overpowered in his affair. So how could you follow him?

His words: *"Look how they strike for you the parables"*: that is, look, O our Messenger, at how these obstinate polytheists have struck for you the parables, saying about you: "a sorcerer," "a poet," "a soothsayer," and "a madman." *"So they have gone astray"* on their path, *"and they cannot find a way"*: they are unable to escape the bewilderment into which their disbelief and obstinacy have cast them.

Guidance from the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- Establishing the principle that love of a thing blinds and deafens: the veil mentioned in the verse, likewise the coverings and the heaviness in the ears, all these prevented them from hearing the Qur'an, because of their hatred of the Messenger ﷺ, of the Qur'an, and of what he brought of the call to monotheism.

2- Clarifying the extent of the polytheists' aversion to monotheism and to the word of sincerity, "There is no god but God."

3- Clarifying the extent of the mockery and ridicule the polytheists directed at the Messenger and the Qur'an.

4- Explaining the accusations the polytheists made against the Messenger ﷺ: sorcery at one time, soothsaying at another, and madness a third time, in search of a way out of the call to monotheism, yet they found nothing, as God Most High says: *"So they have gone astray, and they cannot find a way."*

His words: *"Look how they strike for you the parables"*: that is, look, O our Messenger, at how these obstinate polytheists have struck for you the parables, saying about you: "a sorcerer," "a poet," "a soothsayer," and "a madman." *"So they have gone astray"* on their path, *"and they cannot find a way"*: they are unable to escape the bewilderment into which their disbelief and obstinacy have cast them.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on Surah 17 (al-Isra'), verses 49–52:

Explanation of the words:

﴿And they say: "When we are bones and crumbled particles, shall we indeed be resurrected as a new creation?"﴾ The interrogative is for disbelief and remote improbability. Ruf̄āt (crumbled particles) means scattered pieces.

﴿Something that is greater in your breasts﴾: that is, something that is too great, in your belief, to accept life.

﴿Who originated you﴾: who created you.

﴿They will shake their heads at you﴾: that is, they will shake their heads in amazement.

﴿When is it?﴾: the interrogative is for mockery, meaning: when is this resurrection that you threaten us with?

﴿The Day He calls you﴾: that is, calls you out of your graves through the voice of Isrāfīl.

﴿And you will respond﴾: that is, you will answer His call, saying: "Glory be to You, O Allah, and praise be to You."

﴿And you will think that you remained not but a little﴾: and you will think that you did not remain in your graves except for a little while.

The meaning of the verses:

The context continues to establish the creed. The verses before these established tawhid and revelation, and these verses establish the resurrection and the afterlife recompense. In verse [47], Allah informs of the disbelievers' denial of the resurrection and their remote consideration of it, with His saying: ﴿And they say: "When we are bones and crumbled particles?"﴾, meaning scattered pieces like debris, ﴿shall we indeed be resurrected as a new creation?﴾. In the second verse [48], Allah commands His Messenger ﷺ to say to them: be what you will, for Allah is capable of giving you life and resurrecting you for reckoning and recompense. This is His saying: ﴿Say: "Be stones or iron, or a creation of what is greater in your breasts"﴾, that is, of what is too great in your souls to accept life, like death for example, for Allah will give you life and resurrect you. And His saying: ﴿They will say: "Who will restore us?"﴾ Allah informs His Messenger that the deniers of resurrection will say to him, considering resurrection remote: "Who will restore us?" And He knew the answer, so He said to him: ﴿Say: "He who originated you"﴾, that is, created you the first time. This is a silencing answer: the One who created you and then caused you to die is the One who will restore you as He originated you, and it is easier for Him. His saying: ﴿They will shake their heads at you and say, "When is it?"﴾ Allah informs His Messenger of what the deniers of resurrection will say to him: ﴿They will shake their heads at you﴾, that is, they will move their heads toward you, lowering and raising them in mockery, and say: ﴿When is it?﴾, that is, when is the resurrection, on what day will it occur. His saying: ﴿Say: "Perhaps it is near"﴾ teaches him how to answer the deniers. His saying: ﴿The Day He calls you and you will respond, praising Him, and you will think you remained not but a little﴾ means your resurrection which you deny will be on the day Allah commands Isrāfīl to call you from your graves, and you will respond, that is, you will answer him, praising Allah, ﴿and you will think you remained not but a little﴾, that is, you did not remain in your graves except a little while, because of the terrors you witness and the frightening, horrifying conditions you see.

Guidance from the verses:

1- Establishing the creed of resurrection and recompense and clarifying its certainty.

2- Explaining the extent of the disbelievers' intense denial of the final resurrection.

3- Allah teaches His Messenger how to answer deniers who mock, with that which is best.

4- Clarifying the gentle, dialogic manner free of harshness and severity.

5- Perceiving the duration of the stay in the graves as short, despite its length, because of the terrors of the resurrection that are witnessed.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 17, verses 53–55:

Explanation of the words:

*Allati hiya ahsan* (the word that is better): i.e., the word that is better than others for its gentleness and goodness.

*Yanzagh* (sows discord): i.e., corrupts relations between them.

*Aduwwan mubinan* (a manifest enemy): i.e., clearly hostile, its enmity evident.

*Rabbukum a'lamu bikum* (your Lord knows you best): this is the word that is better.

*Wa ma arsalnaka 'alayhim wakilan* (We did not send you as a guardian over them): i.e., it is not incumbent upon you to compel them to faith.

*Faddalna ba'da al-nabiyyin* (We preferred some of the prophets): i.e., by singling out each of them with particular virtues or a distinctive excellence.

*Wa atayna Dawuda Zabura* (and We gave David the Psalms): i.e., a book called the Zabur; this is a form of preference.

Meaning of the verses:

The context continues to seek the guidance of the people of Makkah through dialogue and argument. It happened that some believers, during debate with some disbelievers, spoke harshly, such as threatening them with the punishment of the Fire, and this stirred the indignation of the polytheists. So God commanded His Messenger to tell the believers that when they address the polytheists, they should not speak to them harshly. God said: ﴿And say to My servants﴾, i.e., the believers, ﴿that they should speak in the way that is best﴾ among words, so that they may find a path to the hearts of the disbelievers. God gave the reason for this, saying: ﴿Indeed, Satan sows discord among them﴾ through whispering, which corrupts the bonds through which guidance of the astray could have been reached. Satan has been, and still is, a manifest enemy to man, i.e., his enmity is clearly apparent: he does not want the disbeliever to become Muslim, nor does he want the Muslim to be rewarded and recompensed for his call. And God's saying: ﴿Your Lord knows you best. If He wills, He will have mercy upon you﴾ by turning to you in repentance so that you become Muslims, ﴿or if He wills, He will punish you﴾ by leaving you to die in your polytheism so that you enter the Fire. Such speech is what the believers should say to the disbelievers, not pass judgment on them that they are people of the Fire and abiding in it, which would distress the polytheists so that they persist in obstinacy and arrogance. And God's saying: ﴿And We did not send you as a guardian over them﴾. God says to His Messenger: We did not send you as a watcher over them so that you would compel them to Islam; rather We sent you as a conveyor of Our call to them with the goodly manner and to guide them to Us. In this is an instruction for the believers on how to invite the disbelievers to Islam. And God's saying: ﴿And your Lord knows best who is in the heavens and the earth﴾ informs His Messenger and the believers implicitly that He is the most knowing of who is in the heavens and the earth, let alone these polytheists. He knows best what suits them and what has been decreed for them, whether happiness or misery, and the causes of that, whether faith or disbelief. Therefore, do not grieve over their denial, do not despair of their faith, and do not burden yourselves with what you cannot bear in guiding them. Say the best word and leave the matter of their guidance to God, who is their Lord and knows them best. And God's saying: ﴿And We have certainly preferred some of the prophets over others, and We gave David the Psalms﴾ informs of His favor among His servants. He who preferred among the prophets, and He is the most perfect and purest of creation: this is His favor by intimate friendship, as with Abraham; this by direct speech, as with Moses; and this by a book full of glorification, praise, lessons, and admonitions, as with David. And you, O Muhammad, by His forgiveness of what preceded and what followed of your sins, and by sending you to all people, along with other bounties. When this truth becomes clear to you and you know that God knows best who deserves guidance and who deserves misguidance, and likewise mercy and punishment, then entrust the matter to Him, and call His servants with gentleness and softness, and with the word that is best among words.

Lessons of the verses:

Among the lessons of the verses:

1- The prohibition of harsh, offensive speech toward one invited to Islam.

2- The clarification that Satan always strives to cause corruption, so he is not given opportunity through words that provoke anger and lead to stubborn obstinacy and fierce quarrelling.

3- The clarification of the kind of word that is best, such as ﴿Your Lord knows you best. If He wills, He will have mercy upon you, or if He wills, He will punish you﴾.

4- The clarification that God, exalted is He, knows His creation best, so He grants each servant what He has qualified him for, even to the extent that He preferred among His prophets and messengers, peace be upon them, in spiritual perfections and lofty ranks.

The context continues to seek the guidance of the people of Makkah through dialogue and argument. It happened that some believers, during debate with some disbelievers, spoke harshly, such as threatening them with the punishment of the Fire, and this stirred the indignation of the polytheists. God said: ﴿And say to My servants﴾, i.e., the believers, ﴿that they should speak in the way that is best﴾ among words, so that they may find a path to the hearts of the disbelievers. God gave the reason for this, saying: ﴿Indeed, Satan sows discord among them﴾ through whispering, which corrupts the bonds through which guidance of the astray could have been reached.
