Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 17, verse 56–60:

Explanation of the words:

"فلا يملكون" (fa-la yamlikun): i.e., they are not able.

"كشف الضر" (kashf al-durr): i.e., removing it by curing the sick person.

"ولا تحويلا" (wa-la tahwilan): i.e., transferring the illness from a sick person to a healthy one so that the healthy one falls ill with it.

"يدعون" (yad'un): i.e., they call out to them, seeking from them or appealing to them (tawassul).

"يبتغون إلى ربهم الوسيلة" (yabtaghuna ila rabbihim al-wasilah): i.e., they seek nearness to Him through acts of obedience and various kinds of devotion (qurbat).

"كان محذورا" (kana mahdhuran): i.e., it is something the believers beware of and guard against by abandoning the disobedience of Allah, the Exalted.

"في الكتاب مسطورا" (fi al-kitab masturan): i.e., written in the Book of Decrees, which is the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz).

"أن نرسل بالآيات" (an nursil bil-ayat): i.e., with the signs that the people of Makkah requested, such as turning al-Safa into a mountain of gold, or removing the mountains of Makkah so that it becomes farmland, and making springs flow within it.

"إلا أن كذب بها الأولون" (illa an kadhdhaba biha al-awwalun): when the people of Salih asked for a sign, and when it came to them they disbelieved in it, so Allah, the Exalted, destroyed them.

"الناقة مبصرة" (al-naqata mubsirah): i.e., We gave Thamud, the people of Salih, the she-camel as a clear, evident sign.

"فظلموا بها" (fa-zalamu biha): i.e., they disbelieved in it and denied it, so Allah, the Exalted, destroyed them.

"إلا تخويفا" (illa takhwifan): only for the sake of frightening the servants, that if We give them signs and they do not believe, We destroy them.

"أحاط بالناس" (ahata bi al-nas): i.e., in power and knowledge, so they are in His grip and under His authority, so do not fear them.

"وما جعلنا الرؤيا" (wa-ma ja'alna al-ru'ya): it is what the Messenger ﷺ saw on the night of the Isra' and Mi'raj of the wonders of Allah's creation.

"والشجرة الملعونة" (wa-al-shajarah al-mal'unah): it is the tree of zaqqum, whose name is mentioned in al-Saffat and al-Dukhan.

"ونخوفهم" (wa-nukhawwifuhum): with Our punishment in this world by destruction and annihilation, and in the Hereafter with the zaqqum and the painful punishment.

"فما يزيدهم" (fa-ma yaziduhum): i.e., the frightening only increases them in transgression (tughyan) and disbelief.

Explanation of the verses:

The context continues to establish tawhid. Allah, the Exalted, says to His Messenger: Say, O Muhammad ﷺ, to those polytheists: Call upon those whom you claim to be gods besides Allah, the Exalted. Indeed, they are not able to remove harm from a sick person, nor can they transfer it from him to another enemy who wants to harm him, because they are idols and statues that neither hear nor see, let alone respond to the one who calls upon them to remove harm or transfer it to someone else. This is what the first verse [54] indicates: ﴿Say: Call upon those whom you claim besides Him; they have no power to remove the harm from you, nor to transfer it.﴾

His saying: ﴿Those whom they call upon themselves seek means of access to their Lord, [as to] which of them would be nearest, and they hope for His mercy and fear His punishment.﴾ He informs them that those whom they worship, whether jinn, angels, prophets or righteous people, are themselves calling upon their Lord and seeking the means to attain His pleasure through all kinds of obedience and devotion. The one who is worshipped is not the one who worships; the one who draws near to Allah through acts of obedience is not himself drawn near to, but draws near to the One to whom he draws near, to attain a station with Him. His saying ﴿and they hope for His mercy and fear His punishment﴾ means that those whom the ignorant people call upon and ask to fulfil their needs are themselves seeking Allah, hoping for His mercy and fearing His punishment, because His punishment has always been, and still is, feared by the wise, for it is severe and unbearable.

How can one who calls upon, hopes for, and fears [his Lord] be called upon, hoped for, and feared, if the polytheists had any understanding?

His saying: ﴿And there is no city but that We will destroy it before the Day of Resurrection or punish it with a severe punishment﴾, i.e., a city among the cities, ﴿but that We will destroy it before the Day of Resurrection with a destroying punishment, or punish it with a severe punishment by sickness, famine, or fear of an enemy﴾, ﴿that is in the Book inscribed﴾, i.e., written in the Preserved Tablet. Therefore the people of Makkah should not seek to hasten the punishment: if it has been decreed for them, it will certainly befall them, and if it has not been decreed for them, there is no point in hastening it, for it will not come upon them, and they are awaited to repent or to the punishment of the Day of Resurrection.

His saying: ﴿And We did not refrain from sending the signs﴾, i.e., the miracles and extraordinary signs, ﴿except that the former peoples denied them﴾, i.e., the former nations denied the miracles, so We destroyed them for their denial. Had We sent our Prophet Muhammad with the like of those signs and Quraysh denied them, We would have destroyed them. He, the Exalted, does not desire their destruction, but desires their guidance, so that through them a great number of Arabs and non-Arabs, whites and yellows, may be guided. Glory be to Allah, the All-Knowing, the All-Wise.

His saying: ﴿And We gave Thamud the she-camel as a visible sign﴾, i.e., a clear, illuminating, evident sign, ﴿but they wronged themselves by it﴾, i.e., they denied it, so they hamstrung it, thereby wronging themselves and exposing themselves to the punishment of annihilation, so Allah annihilated them; the Cry seized them while they were wrongdoers. This is evidence that what prevents the sending of signs is what Allah, the Exalted, mentioned in this verse.

His saying: ﴿And We do not send the signs except as a warning﴾: He, the Exalted, informs that He does not send Messengers supported by signs, which are miracles, lessons and admonitions, except to warn people of the consequence of disbelief and disobedience, so that they may fear, believe and obey.

His saying: ﴿And [remember] when We said to you, "Indeed, your Lord has encompassed the people"﴾, i.e., remember, O Muhammad, when We said to you through this revelation that your Lord has encompassed the people. They are in His grasp and under His subjugation and authority, so do not dread them and do not fear any of them, for Allah is your helper against them, and the sender of His vengeance upon whoever persists in wrongdoing and obstinacy.

His saying: ﴿And We did not make the vision which We showed you﴾ refers to the vision of the Isra' and Mi'raj, in which Allah showed him some of His signs and wonders of His creation, ﴿except as a trial for the people﴾, i.e., a test for the people of Makkah, to see whether they would believe or deny it, since it is not necessary for establishing your prophethood and confirming your messengership and your excellence that We show you the supreme realm and what it contains of manifestations of power, knowledge, wisdom and mercy.

His saying: ﴿And the cursed tree [in the Qur'an]﴾, i.e., We did not make the cursed tree mentioned in the Noble Qur'an, which is the tree of zaqqum, which ﴿emerges from the root of Hellfire﴾ [al-Saffat: 64], except as a trial as well for the people of Makkah, when they said: how can a palm tree bearing fruit exist in the midst of fire, and why does the fire not burn it? They were analogizing the unseen to the seen, and that is a faulty analogy. His saying: ﴿And We warn them﴾ with the cursed tree, that it is ﴿the food of the sinner, like murky oil, boiling in the bellies like the boiling of scalding water﴾ [al-Dukhan: 44-46], and with other kinds of worldly and otherworldly punishment. But this only increases them in great transgression, i.e., exaltation and arrogance against accepting the truth and responding to it, because of what has already been decreed in Allah's knowledge regarding their disgrace and punishment. So be patient, O Messenger, and continue in your call, for the final outcome is yours.

Guidance from the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- Establishing tawhid by judging that the deities invoked cannot answer their worshippers.

2- Clarifying a rational truth: that calling upon the saints, seeking aid from them, and approaching them through sacrifice and vows is a false matter and simultaneously ridiculous, since the saints, before their death, were seeking the means to their Lord through various kinds of obedience and devotion. Whoever worshipped is not worshipped; whoever drew near is not drawn near to; whoever sought means is not sought by means; rather, one worships the One who was worshipped, and seeks means to the One to whom they sought means, and draws near to the One to whom they drew near, namely Allah, the Exalted.

3- Affirming the doctrine of divine decree and predestination (al-qada' wa-al-qadar).

4- Explaining the reason why the Messenger ﷺ was not given the signs that Quraysh asked for.

5- Explaining the purpose of the Isra' and Mi'raj, and mentioning the tree of zaqqum in the Noble Qur'an.

"الناقة مبصرة" (al-naqata mubsirah): i.e., We gave Thamud, the people of Salih, the she-camel as a clear, evident sign.

"فظلموا بها" (fa-zalamu biha): i.e., they disbelieved in it and denied it, so Allah, the Exalted, destroyed them.

"إلا تخويفا" (illa takhwifan): only for the sake of frightening the servants, that if We give them signs and they do not believe, We destroy them.

"أحاط بالناس" (ahata bi al-nas): i.e., in power and knowledge, so they are in His grip and under His authority, so do not fear them.

"وما جعلنا الرؤيا" (wa-ma ja'alna al-ru'ya): it is what the Messenger ﷺ saw on the night of the Isra' and Mi'raj of the wonders of Allah's creation.

"والشجرة الملعونة" (wa-al-shajarah al-mal'unah): it is the tree of zaqqum, whose name is mentioned in al-Saffat and al-Dukhan.

"ونخوفهم" (wa-nukhawwifuhum): with Our punishment in this world by destruction and annihilation, and in the Hereafter with the zaqqum and the painful punishment.

"فما يزيدهم" (fa-ma yaziduhum): i.e., the frightening only increases them in transgression (tughyan) and disbelief.

Explanation of the verses:

The context continues to establish tawhid. Allah, the Exalted, says to His Messenger: Say, O Muhammad ﷺ, to those polytheists: Call upon those whom you claim to be gods besides Allah, the Exalted. Indeed, they are not able to remove harm from a sick person, nor can they transfer it from him to another enemy who wants to harm him, because they are idols and statues that neither hear nor see, let alone respond to the one who calls upon them to remove harm or transfer it to someone else. This is what the first verse [54] indicates: ﴿Say: Call upon those whom you claim besides Him; they have no power to remove the harm from you, nor to transfer it.﴾

His saying: ﴿Those whom they call upon themselves seek means of access to their Lord, [as to] which of them would be nearest, and they hope for His mercy and fear His punishment.﴾ He informs them that those whom they worship, whether jinn, angels, prophets or righteous people, are themselves calling upon their Lord and seeking the means to attain His pleasure through all kinds of obedience and devotion. The one who is worshipped is not the one who worships; the one who draws near to Allah through acts of obedience is not himself drawn near to, but draws near to the One to whom he draws near, to attain a station with Him. His saying ﴿and they hope for His mercy and fear His punishment﴾ means that those whom the ignorant people call upon and ask to fulfil their needs are themselves seeking Allah, hoping for His mercy and fearing His punishment, because His punishment has always been, and still is, feared by the wise, for it is severe and unbearable.

How can one who calls upon, hopes for, and fears [his Lord] be called upon, hoped for, and feared, if the polytheists had any understanding?

His saying: ﴿And there is no city but that We will destroy it before the Day of Resurrection or punish it with a severe punishment﴾, i.e., a city among the cities, ﴿but that We will destroy it before the Day of Resurrection with a destroying punishment, or punish it with a severe punishment by sickness, famine, or fear of an enemy﴾, ﴿that is in the Book inscribed﴾, i.e., written in the Preserved Tablet. Therefore the people of Makkah should not seek to hasten the punishment: if it has been decreed for them, it will certainly befall them, and if it has not been decreed for them, there is no point in hastening it, for it will not come upon them, and they are awaited to repent or to the punishment of the Day of Resurrection.

His saying: ﴿And We did not refrain from sending the signs﴾, i.e., the miracles and extraordinary signs, ﴿except that the former peoples denied them﴾, i.e., the former nations denied the miracles, so We destroyed them for their denial. Had We sent our Prophet Muhammad with the like of those signs and Quraysh denied them, We would have destroyed them. He, the Exalted, does not desire their destruction, but desires their guidance, so that through them a great number of Arabs and non-Arabs, whites and yellows, may be guided. Glory be to Allah, the All-Knowing, the All-Wise.

His saying: ﴿And We gave Thamud the she-camel as a visible sign﴾, i.e., a clear, illuminating, evident sign, ﴿but they wronged themselves by it﴾, i.e., they denied it, so they hamstrung it, thereby wronging themselves and exposing themselves to the punishment of annihilation, so Allah annihilated them; the Cry seized them while they were wrongdoers. This is evidence that what prevents the sending of signs is what Allah, the Exalted, mentioned in this verse.

His saying: ﴿And We do not send the signs except as a warning﴾: He, the Exalted, informs that He does not send Messengers supported by signs, which are miracles, lessons and admonitions, except to warn people of the consequence of disbelief and disobedience, so that they may fear, believe and obey.

His saying: ﴿And [remember] when We said to you, "Indeed, your Lord has encompassed the people"﴾, i.e., remember, O Muhammad, when We said to you through this revelation that your Lord has encompassed the people. They are in His grasp and under His subjugation and authority, so do not dread them and do not fear any of them, for Allah is your helper against them, and the sender of His vengeance upon whoever persists in wrongdoing and obstinacy.

His saying: ﴿And We did not make the vision which We showed you﴾ refers to the vision of the Isra' and Mi'raj, in which Allah showed him some of His signs and wonders of His creation, ﴿except as a trial for the people﴾, i.e., a test for the people of Makkah, to see whether they would believe or deny it, since it is not necessary for establishing your prophethood and confirming your messengership and your excellence that We show you the supreme realm and what it contains of manifestations of power, knowledge, wisdom and mercy.

His saying: ﴿And the cursed tree [in the Qur'an]﴾, i.e., We did not make the cursed tree mentioned in the Noble Qur'an, which is the tree of zaqqum, which ﴿emerges from the root of Hellfire﴾ [al-Saffat: 64], except as a trial as well for the people of Makkah, when they said: how can a palm tree bearing fruit exist in the midst of fire, and why does the fire not burn it? His saying: ﴿And We warn them﴾ with the cursed tree, that it is ﴿the food of the sinner, like murky oil, boiling in the bellies like the boiling of scalding water﴾ [al-Dukhan: 44-46], and with other kinds of worldly and otherworldly punishment. But this only increases them in great transgression, i.e., exaltation and arrogance against accepting the truth and responding to it, because of what has already been decreed in Allah's knowledge regarding their disgrace and punishment. So be patient, O Messenger, and continue in your call, for the final outcome is yours.

Guidance from the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- Establishing tawhid by judging that the deities invoked cannot answer their worshippers.

2- Clarifying a rational truth: that calling upon the saints, seeking aid from them, and approaching them through sacrifice and vows is a false matter and simultaneously ridiculous, since the saints, before their death, were seeking the means to their Lord through various kinds of obedience and devotion. Whoever worshipped is not worshipped; whoever drew near is not drawn near to; whoever sought means is not sought by means; rather, one worships the One who was worshipped, and seeks means to the One to whom they sought means, and draws near to the One to whom they drew near, namely Allah, the Exalted.

3- Affirming the doctrine of divine decree and predestination (al-qada' wa-al-qadar).

4- Explaining the reason why the Messenger ﷺ was not given the signs that Quraysh asked for.

5- Explaining the purpose of the Isra' and Mi'raj, and mentioning the tree of zaqqum in the Noble Qur'an.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 17, verses 61–65:

Explanation of the words:

*Liman khalaqta tinan* (﴿لمن خلقت طيناً﴾): i.e., from clay.

*Ara'aytak* (﴿أرأيتك﴾): i.e., tell me.

*Karramta 'alayya* (﴿كرمت علي﴾): i.e., you preferred him over me by commanding me to prostrate to him.

*La-ahtanikanna* (﴿لأحتنكن﴾): I will certainly take control of them and lead them into misguidance, like a beast when a halter is put on its jaw, led wherever its rider wishes!

*Idhhab* (﴿اذهب﴾): i.e., you are granted respite until the time of the first blast.

*Jaza'an mawfuran* (﴿جزاءً موفوراً﴾): i.e., full and complete recompense.

*Bi-sawtika* (﴿بصوتك﴾): i.e., by your calling them to obedience to you and disobedience to Me, with the sounds of flutes, songs and amusement.

*Wa-ajlib 'alayhim* (﴿وأجلب عليهم﴾): i.e., shout at them with your riders and your foot soldiers.

*Wa-shariknhum fi al-amwal* (﴿وشاركهم في الأموال﴾): by inciting them to consume and engage in usury (riba).

*La-ahtanikanna* (﴿لأحتنكن﴾): I will certainly take control of them and lead them into misguidance, like a beast when a halter is put on its jaw, led wherever its rider wishes!

*Idhhab* (﴿اذهب﴾): i.e., you are granted respite until the time of the first blast.

*Jaza'an mawfuran* (﴿جزاءً موفوراً﴾): i.e., full and complete recompense.

*Bi-sawtika* (﴿بصوتك﴾): i.e., by your calling them to obedience to you and disobedience to Me, with the sounds of flutes, songs and amusement.

*Wa-ajlib 'alayhim* (﴿وأجلب عليهم﴾): i.e., shout at them with your riders and your foot soldiers.

*Wa-shariknhum fi al-amwal* (﴿وشاركهم في الأموال﴾): by inciting them to consume and engage in usury (riba).

*Wal-awlad* (﴿والأولاد﴾): by adorning fornication (zina) for them and pushing them towards it.

*Wa'iduhum* (﴿وعدهم﴾): i.e., by promising them that there is no resurrection, no reckoning and no requital.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 17, verses 66–70:

Explanation of the words:

Yuzji lakumu al-fulk (يزجي لكم الفلك): i.e., drives it along, so that it moves through the sea.

Li-tabtaghu min fadlihi (لتبتغوا من فضله): i.e., so that you may seek God's provision through trade, from one region to another.

Wa-idha massakumu al-durr (وإذا مسكم الضُر): i.e., hardship, affliction, and fear of drowning.

Ḍalla man tad'una illa iyyah (ضل من تدعون إلا إياه): i.e., those you used to call upon, your gods, have vanished from you.

A'radtum (أعرضتم): i.e., you turned away from calling upon God and affirming His oneness in that matter.

Aw yursila 'alaykum ḥasiban (أو يرسل عليكم حاصباً): i.e., a wind that hurls pebbles because of its intensity.

Thumma la tajidu lakum wakilan (ثم لا تجدوا لكم وكيلاً): i.e., a protector from Him, that is, from the sinking of the land or the pebble-laden wind.

Qasifan min al-rih (قاصفاً من الريح): i.e., a violent wind that shatters and breaks trees by its force.

'Alayna bihi tabi'an (علينا به تبيعاً): i.e., a helper and supporter who follows us to avenge you against us.

Wa-laqad karramna Bani Adam (ولقد كرمنا بني آدم): i.e., We favored them with knowledge, speech, and balanced creation.

Ḥamalnahum fi al-barr wal-bahr (حملناهم في البر والبحر): on land upon beasts, and at sea upon ships.

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues to affirm the oneness of God and to call to it. God's words, ﴿Your Lord is He who drives the ship for you through the sea, that you may seek of His bounty﴾, inform them that their true Lord, whom they must worship and obey after believing, is the One who ﴿drives the ship for you﴾, that is, the vessel, ﴿in the sea﴾, that is, He propels it so that it carries them in the sea wherever they wish, in order that they may seek God's provision for them through trade from one region to another. This is your true God; as for idols and images, they are created by God and subject to Him, possessing nothing for themselves, let alone for others, of benefit or harm.

God's words, ﴿Indeed He is ever Merciful to you﴾, refer to His mercy in subjecting the sea for them and driving the ships in it so that they obtain their sustenance through travel and trade. God's words, ﴿And when harm touches you at sea, those whom you invoke vanish except Him﴾, remind them of a fact that actually happens to them: when they board ships and are struck by hardship, such as sickness, losing the way, or sea storms that toss the ships and make them fear drowning, they call upon God alone, and there is none left to call upon but Him, exalted is He. But when He delivers them from the ruin they feared and brings them ashore to safety, they turn away from the remembrance of God, remember their gods, and forget what they used to call upon, which is God. ﴿And man has ever been ungrateful﴾: this is his nature and his state, swift forgetfulness and great ingratitude. God's words, while addressing them for their guidance: ﴿Do you then feel secure that He will not cause the side of the land to swallow you﴾, rebuke them for their turning away. He says, ﴿Do you then feel secure﴾ from God ﴿that He will cause you to be swallowed﴾ at the side of the land where you landed when you came out of the sea, ﴿or send against you a storm of pebbles﴾, that is, a violent wind carrying pebbles that destroys you as He destroyed ʿAd, ﴿then you will not find for yourselves﴾ apart from God ﴿any guardian﴾ who can avert the punishment from you. And He says, ﴿Or do you feel secure that He will not return you to it﴾ — that is, to the sea — ﴿another time﴾, that is, once more, ﴿and send against you a violent wind that shatters [ships]﴾, that is, a violent wind that shatters and breaks the trees, ﴿and drown you for what you disbelieved﴾, that is, because of your disbelief, as He drowned the family of Pharaoh, ﴿then you will not find for yourselves against Us any pursuer﴾, that is, any follower who will avenge you and pursue us demanding what punishment we have inflicted upon you.

So what is wrong with you, that you do not believe and affirm God's oneness, and instead disbelieve in falsehood? God's words, ﴿And We have certainly honored the children of Adam﴾, that is, We favored them with speech, reason, knowledge, and balanced creation. ﴿And We carried them on land and sea﴾ upon the vehicles We subjected for them. ﴿And We have provided for them of the good things﴾, that is, the delicious foods: meats, grains, fruits, vegetables, and sweet, fresh water. God's words, ﴿And We have preferred them over much of what We have created with [definite] preference﴾: humans are superior to jinn and all other animals; their elite are superior to the angels, while the general body of angels is superior to the general body of humans. Yet if a human disbelieves in his Lord, associates another in His worship, abandons His worship, and empties his heart of His love and vigilance, he becomes the worst of all creation. God says: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieved among the People of the Scripture and the polytheists will be in the fire of Hell, abiding eternally therein. They are the worst of creatures﴾ [al-Bayyinah: 6].

From the guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of the verses:

1- Making God known through the mention of His active and essential attributes.

2- Reminding the polytheists of their state in hardship and ease, for they recognize God in hardship and sincerely direct their supplication to Him, yet deny Him in ease and associate others with Him.

3- Warning the polytheists that God is able to cause the earth to swallow them, or send against them a pebble-laden wind that destroys them, or return them to the sea and send against them a shattering wind that drowns them for their disbelief in God and their return to polytheism after calling upon Him and humbling themselves to Him in hardship.

4- Explaining God's bounties and favors upon humankind in honoring and preferring them.

5- The state of ease is harder for people than the state of hardship through famine, illness, or other calamities.

6- Proclaiming the dignity and nobility of the human being over all other creatures on earth.

**Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on Surah 17, Verses 71–77**

**Explanation of the Words:**

*Bi-imamihim* (with their leader): that is, the one whom they used to follow and take as a model, for good or for evil.

*Fatilan* (a speck): that is, the measure of a *fatil*, which is the thread found in the middle of a date pit.

*Wa man kana fi hadhihi a'ma* (and whoever was blind in this [life]): whoever was blind in this world to the proofs of God Most High that indicate His existence, knowledge and power, so that he did not believe in Him or worship Him, will be even more blind in the Hereafter and further astray from the way.

*Wa in kadu* (and they almost): that is, they came close to.

*Liyaftinunaka* (to tempt you): that is, they seek to make you give up the truth, that is, they seek your withdrawal from it.

*Litaftari 'alayna ghayrahu* (so that you would invent against Us other than it): that is, so that you would say about Us a fabrication other than what We revealed to you.

*Idhan la-attakhadhukum khalilan* (then they would have taken you as a close friend): that is, if you had done what they asked you to do, they would have taken you as their friend.

*Did al-hayati wa did al-mamati* (double [punishment] of life and double [punishment] of death): that is, We would have made you suffer the punishment of this world doubled, and the punishment of the Hereafter likewise.

*Liyastafizzunaka min al-ardi* (they would surely drive you out of the land): that is, they would expel you from the land, the land of Makkah.

*La yalbathuna khilafaka illa qalilan* (they would not remain after you except a little): that is, they would not remain behind you, after you, except for a little while, and God would destroy them.

*Sunnata man qad arsalna qablaka* (the way of those whom We sent before you): that is, if they had expelled you, We would have punished them shortly after your departure; this is Our way with the nations.

*Wa la tajidu lisunnatina tahwilan* (and you will not find any change in Our way): that is, in what has taken place among the earlier nations.

**Meaning of the Verses:**

God Most High says to His Messenger, in establishing the belief in resurrection and recompense: mention, O Our Messenger, ﴿the Day when We will call every people with their leader﴾, whom they used to follow and take as a model. The leader will go forward, with his followers behind him, and the books will be distributed to them one by one. Whoever is given his book in his right hand, as an honour and a mark of dignity, those are the ones who were honoured by being given their books in their right hands. They will read their book and be reckoned by what is in it, ﴿and they will not be wronged﴾, that is, they will not have any good deed diminished even by the measure of a speck, nor will their evil deeds be increased. Mention this to them so that they may be admonished by it, perhaps they will take heed.

His saying, ﴿And whoever was in this [life] blind﴾, that is, in this world, ﴿blind﴾, not seeing these proofs, signs and evidences, and persisting in *shirk* (associating partners with God), denial and sins, ﴿he will be in the Hereafter blind﴾, that is, even more blind, ﴿and further astray from the way﴾, so he will not see the path of salvation nor follow it until he falls into Hell.

His saying: ﴿And they almost tempted you﴾, that is, they would divert you ﴿from that which We have revealed to you﴾ of Our monotheism, and from rejecting falsehood and its people. ﴿So that you would invent against Us other than it﴾, that is, so that you would say about Us something other than the truth We revealed to you. ﴿And then they would have taken you as a close friend﴾, that is, if you had done so, by agreeing to what they asked of you, such as overlooking their polytheism and being tolerant with them, thereby affirming their falsehood, even if only temporarily, ﴿they would have taken you as a friend﴾ for them, and they would have been your allies. This is because the polytheists in Makkah and Ta'if, and the Jews in Madinah, were doing their utmost to bring the Messenger down to some concession from the truth which he commanded and called to, through cunning and political deception. For if he had agreed with them on something, they would have demanded something else and said, "He has returned to us; therefore he is inventing [the revelation], and he is not one to whom revelation is sent," as evidenced by his acceptance of such and such from us and his giving up of such and such.

His saying, ﴿And had We not made you firm﴾, that is, in the truth, by protecting you, ﴿you would nearly have inclined﴾, that is, you would have come close to ﴿inclining towards them a little﴾, by accepting some of their proposals, ﴿then﴾, that is, if you had inclined to them and accepted from them even a little, ﴿We would have made you taste double [punishment] of life and double of death﴾. That is, We would have doubled the punishment upon you in this world and the Hereafter, ﴿then you would not find for yourself any helper to support you﴾ if We forsook you and punished you.

His saying, concerning another incident: when they failed in their peaceful attempts, they wanted to use force, and they resolved to expel him from Makkah, whether dead or alive. God Most High therefore informed His Messenger of this, as a notice and a warning, saying: ﴿And they almost sought to unsettle you from the land﴾, the land of Makkah, ﴿to expel you from it. Then they would not remain [there] after you except for a little﴾, that is, if they had done so, they would not have remained after your expulsion except for a short time, and We would have destroyed them, as is Our way with the earlier nations that expelled their prophets or killed them. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿And they almost sought to unsettle you﴾, that is, to make you light [in their eyes] ﴿from the land to expel you from it. Then they would not remain after you except for a little, [as] the way of those whom We sent before you of Our messengers. And you will not find any change in Our way﴾, that is, in what has taken place among the earlier nations.

**Guidance of the Verses:**

**From the guidance of the verses:**

1. Encouragement to take righteous people as models and to follow them, and warning against taking the people of corruption as models and following them.
2. God's justice on the Day of Standing, by establishing the proof against the servant and not wronging him in anything.
3. Blindness to the truth and its signs in this world is the cause of blindness in the Hereafter and of what brings about falling into Hell.
4. The prohibition of *rukun* (inclining) towards the people of falsehood, by giving up some of the established truth to please them.
5. Severe warning against whoever pleases the people of falsehood by flattery, seeking their worldly gains, and so abandons the truth for their sake.
6. The enforcement of God's ways and their not being changed under any circumstances.

His saying, ﴿And whoever was in this [life] blind﴾, that is, in this world, ﴿blind﴾, not seeing these proofs, signs and evidences, and persisting in *shirk* (associating partners with God), denial and sins, ﴿he will be in the Hereafter blind﴾, that is, even more blind, ﴿and further astray from the way﴾, so he will not see the path of salvation nor follow it until he falls into Hell.

His saying: ﴿And they almost tempted you﴾, that is, they would divert you ﴿from that which We have revealed to you﴾ of Our monotheism, and from rejecting falsehood and its people. ﴿So that you would invent against Us other than it﴾, that is, so that you would say about Us something other than the truth We revealed to you. ﴿And then they would have taken you as a close friend﴾, that is, if you had done so, by agreeing to what they asked of you, such as overlooking their polytheism and being tolerant with them, thereby affirming their falsehood, even if only temporarily, ﴿they would have taken you as a friend﴾ for them, and they would have been your allies. This is because the polytheists in Makkah and Ta'if, and the Jews in Madinah, were doing their utmost to bring the Messenger down to some concession from the truth which he commanded and called to, through cunning and political deception. For if he had agreed with them on something, they would have demanded something else and said, "He has returned to us; therefore he is inventing [the revelation], and he is not one to whom revelation is sent," as evidenced by his acceptance of such and such from us and his giving up of such and such.

His saying, concerning another incident: when they failed in their peaceful attempts, they wanted to use force, and they resolved to expel him from Makkah, whether dead or alive. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿And they almost sought to unsettle you﴾, that is, to make you light [in their eyes] ﴿from the land to expel you from it. **Guidance of the Verses:**

**From the guidance of the verses:**

1. Encouragement to take righteous people as models and to follow them, and warning against taking the people of corruption as models and following them.
2. God's justice on the Day of Standing, by establishing the proof against the servant and not wronging him in anything.
3. Blindness to the truth and its signs in this world is the cause of blindness in the Hereafter and of what brings about falling into Hell.
4. The prohibition of *rukun* (inclining) towards the people of falsehood, by giving up some of the established truth to please them.
5. Severe warning against whoever pleases the people of falsehood by flattery, seeking their worldly gains, and so abandons the truth for their sake.
6. The enforcement of God's ways and their not being changed under any circumstances.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 17, verses 78–84:

Explanation of the words:

*Wa-Qur'ān al-fajr* (and the recitation of dawn): the dawn prayer (ṣalāt al-ṣubḥ).

*Kāna mashhūdan* (it is witnessed): it is witnessed by the angels, the angels of the night and the angels of the day.

*Fa-tahajjad bihi* (so keep vigil with it): i.e., with the Qur'an.

*Nāfilah* (a supererogatory act): i.e., beyond what is obligatory, namely the night vigil (tahajjud).

*Maqāman maḥmūdan* (a praiseworthy station): this is the Great Intercession (al-shafā'ah al-ʿuẓmā) on the Day of Resurrection, whereby the first and the last of creation will praise him.

*Adkhilnī madkhala ṣidq* (cause me to enter with a sound entry): i.e., Medina, an entry that is pleasing, in which I see nothing disagreeable.

*Wa-akhrijnī makhraja ṣidq* (and cause me to exit with a sound exit): i.e., from Mecca, an exit in which my heart does not turn back toward it.

*Wa-qul jā'a al-ḥaqq wa-zahaq al-bāṭil* (and say: the truth has come and falsehood has vanished): i.e., upon your entering Mecca as a conqueror of it by God's permission, the Exalted.

*Zahaqa al-bāṭil* (falsehood vanished): i.e., it departed and was utterly effaced.

*Aʿraḍa wa-nā bi-jānibihi* (he turned away and withdrew his side): he turned away from gratitude and did not give thanks; *nā bi-jānibihi* means he bent his side, strutting in arrogance.

*ʿAlā shākilatihi* (according to his own manner): i.e., his way and his doctrine, which conforms to his state in guidance and error.

Meaning of the verses:

After that tremendous display of those momentous events, God the Exalted commanded His Messenger to establish the prayer, for it is the refuge of the fearful, the beacon of those who travel the path, and the ascent of souls to the courtyard of joy. He said: ﴿Establish the prayer at the decline of the sun﴾, i.e., at its first decline, which is its inclination from the midst of the sky toward the west, and this is the time of midday (zawal) and the entry of the time of the noon prayer (ẓuhr). His words ﴿until the darkness of the night﴾ mean until its darkness, and the afternoon prayer ('aṣr) falls between the decline of the sun and the darkness of the night, while the sunset prayer (maghrib) and the night prayer ('ishā') fall within the darkness of the night. His words ﴿and the recitation of dawn﴾ mean the dawn prayer (ṣalāt al-ṣubḥ), and these are the five obligatory prayers upon the community of Islam, the Prophet and his followers alike. His words ﴿Indeed, the recitation of dawn is ever witnessed﴾ mean attended, the angels of the day attend it so that the angels of the night depart, in accordance with the authentic hadith: "Angels take turns among you by night and by day..." His words ﴿And from the night, keep vigil with it as a supererogatory act for you﴾ mean a prayer in addition to the five obligatory prayers, which is the night vigil (qiyām al-layl). By this verse it is obligatory upon him ﷺ, and for his community it is recommended and desirable.

His words ﴿It may be that your Lord will raise you to a praiseworthy station﴾: "ʿasā" from God the Exalted implies certainty, and therefore God the Exalted informed His Messenger, giving him glad tidings, that He would raise him on the Day of Resurrection to ﴿a praiseworthy station﴾, which the first and the last of creation will praise him for. This is the Great Intercession, when Adam and those after him will withdraw from it, until it reaches him ﷺ, and he says: "I shall take it, I shall take it," and his Lord will permit him to intercede for creation at the judgment, so that the people of Paradise enter Paradise and the people of the Fire enter the Fire, and creation is relieved of the hardship, length, and severity of the standing.

His exalted words ﴿And say: My Lord, cause me to enter with a sound entry and cause me to exit with a sound exit﴾: this is another glad tiding that God the Exalted permitted His Messenger to migrate of his own accord, not by his people expelling him against his will. He said to him: say in your supplication, "My Lord, cause me to enter Medina, the abode of my migration, ﴿with a sound entry﴾, such that I see nothing disagreeable in it, and cause me to exit from Mecca on the day You cause me to exit ﴿with a sound exit﴾, not turning my heart back toward it in longing and yearning."

﴿And grant me from Yourself a supporting authority﴾: i.e., and ask Him to make for you from Himself an authority that will support you against whoever seeks you with harm, plots against you with deceit and treachery, tries to prevent you from establishing your religion and calling to your Lord. His exalted words ﴿And say: The truth has come and falsehood has vanished﴾ are another glad tiding that God the Exalted will open Mecca to him, and he will enter it victorious and triumphant, breaking the idols around the Kaaba, which were three hundred and sixty idols! And he says: "the truth has come and falsehood has vanished," i.e., disbelief has departed and been effaced. ﴿Indeed, falsehood is ever vanishing﴾: it has no permanence and no stability when it confronts the truth and stands against it. It is possible that by "the truth" is meant the Qur'an, and by "falsehood" lies and fabrication; it is also possible that "the truth" is Islam and "falsehood" is disbelief and polytheism, and more generally: the truth is everything that is obedience to God the Mighty and Majestic, and falsehood is every obedience to Satan, including polytheism, wrongdoing, and all other sins.

His exalted words ﴿And We send down of the Qur'an that which is a healing and a mercy for the believers﴾: i.e., and We send down upon you, O Our Messenger Muhammad, from the Qur'an that which is a healing, by which one is cured of the sickness of ignorance, misguidance, doubt, and whisperings, and a mercy for the believers rather than the disbelievers, because the believers act upon it, and God the Exalted shows them mercy by their acting upon His Book. As for the disbelievers, there is no mercy for them in it, because they deny it and abandon acting upon what it contains. His words ﴿and it does not increase the wrongdoers except in loss﴾: i.e., the Qur'an does not increase the wrongdoers, namely the obstinate polytheists who persisted in falsehood out of stubbornness and arrogance, except in loss, because the increase in their disbelief, wrongdoing, and obstinacy comes from what is sent down of the Qur'an that they hear.

His exalted words ﴿And when We bestow favor upon man, he turns away and withdraws his side; and when harm touches him, he is ever despairing﴾: God the Exalted informs about the disbelieving human being, deprived of the light of faith and the guidance of Islam, that when We bestow upon him the blessing of deliverance from destruction, having been brought near to drowning, sickness, hunger, or the like, he turns away from the remembrance of God and His supplication, as he used to supplicate Him in times of hardship, and he withdraws his side, i.e., he goes far from Us and does not turn to Us with his heart, and he goes off in his vanity and pride. His words ﴿and when harm touches him, he is ever despairing﴾ mean in despair (qunūṭ). This is the disbeliever, darkened in soul because of his disbelief and disobedience; when harm touches him, whether hunger, sickness, or fear encompasses him, he is ever very despairing and utterly hopeless, because he has no faith in God, in His mercy, or in His power to save him and deliver him.

His exalted words ﴿Say: Each acts according to his own manner, but your Lord knows best who is best guided on the path﴾: i.e., say, O Our Messenger, to the polytheists: each of us and of you acts according to his own way and doctrine, in accordance with his state of guidance or error. And your Lord, the Exalted, knows best who among us and you is better guided on the path. He will recompense everyone according to his deeds and conduct. This is a decisive word, cutting off the dispute arising from each party claiming to be upon the truth, that its religion is more correct, its way more excellent, and its path more beneficial and profitable.

Guidance of the verses:

1- The obligation of establishing the prayer and the explanation of its appointed times.

2- Encouragement toward supererogatory acts, especially tahajjud, the "night supererogatory prayer."

3- Affirmation of the Great Intercession of the Prophet ﷺ.

4- The weakness of falsehood and its swift vanishing when the truth confronts it and stands against it.

5- The Qur'an is a healing for the diseases of hearts in general and a mercy for the believers in particular.

6- Explanation of the nature of the disbelieving person and the description of the weakness that accompanies him.

7- Teaching the Messenger ﷺ and the believers how to free themselves from empty argument and unproductive debate.

Explanation of the words:

*Li-dulūk al-shams* (at the sun's decline): i.e., its departure from the midst of the sky and its inclination toward the west.

*Ilā ghasaq al-layl* (until the darkness of the night): i.e., until the darkness of night, for *al-ghasaq* means darkness.

*Wa-Qur'ān al-fajr* (and the recitation of dawn): the dawn prayer (ṣalāt al-ṣubḥ).

*Kāna mashhūdan* (it is witnessed): it is witnessed by the angels, the angels of the night and the angels of the day.

*Fa-tahajjad bihi* (so keep vigil with it): i.e., with the Qur'an.

*Nāfilah* (a supererogatory act): i.e., beyond what is obligatory, namely the night vigil (tahajjud).

*Maqāman maḥmūdan* (a praiseworthy station): this is the Great Intercession (al-shafā'ah al-ʿuẓmā) on the Day of Resurrection, whereby the first and the last of creation will praise him.

*Adkhilnī madkhala ṣidq* (cause me to enter with a sound entry): i.e., Medina, an entry that is pleasing, in which I see nothing disagreeable.

*Wa-akhrijnī makhraja ṣidq* (and cause me to exit with a sound exit): i.e., from Mecca, an exit in which my heart does not turn back toward it.

*Wa-qul jā'a al-ḥaqq wa-zahaq al-bāṭil* (and say: the truth has come and falsehood has vanished): i.e., upon your entering Mecca as a conqueror of it by God's permission, the Exalted.

*Zahaqa al-bāṭil* (falsehood vanished): i.e., it departed and was utterly effaced.

*Aʿraḍa wa-nā bi-jānibihi* (he turned away and withdrew his side): he turned away from gratitude and did not give thanks; *nā bi-jānibihi* means he bent his side, strutting in arrogance.

*ʿAlā shākilatihi* (according to his own manner): i.e., his way and his doctrine, which conforms to his state in guidance and error.

Meaning of the verses:

After that tremendous display of those momentous events, God the Exalted commanded His Messenger to establish the prayer, for it is the refuge of the fearful, the beacon of those who travel the path, and the ascent of souls to the courtyard of joy. He said: ﴿Establish the prayer at the decline of the sun﴾, i.e., at its first decline, which is its inclination from the midst of the sky toward the west, and this is the time of midday (zawal) and the entry of the time of the noon prayer (ẓuhr). His words ﴿until the darkness of the night﴾ mean until its darkness, and the afternoon prayer ('aṣr) falls between the decline of the sun and the darkness of the night, while the sunset prayer (maghrib) and the night prayer ('ishā') fall within the darkness of the night. His words ﴿and the recitation of dawn﴾ mean the dawn prayer (ṣalāt al-ṣubḥ), and these are the five obligatory prayers upon the community of Islam, the Prophet and his followers alike. His words ﴿Indeed, the recitation of dawn is ever witnessed﴾ mean attended, the angels of the day attend it so that the angels of the night depart, in accordance with the authentic hadith: "Angels take turns among you by night and by day..." His words ﴿And from the night, keep vigil with it as a supererogatory act for you﴾ mean a prayer in addition to the five obligatory prayers, which is the night vigil (qiyām al-layl). By this verse it is obligatory upon him ﷺ, and for his community it is recommended and desirable.

His words ﴿It may be that your Lord will raise you to a praiseworthy station﴾: "ʿasā" from God the Exalted implies certainty, and therefore God the Exalted informed His Messenger, giving him glad tidings, that He would raise him on the Day of Resurrection to ﴿a praiseworthy station﴾, which the first and the last of creation will praise him for. This is the Great Intercession, when Adam and those after him will withdraw from it, until it reaches him ﷺ, and he says: "I shall take it, I shall take it," and his Lord will permit him to intercede for creation at the judgment, so that the people of Paradise enter Paradise and the people of the Fire enter the Fire, and creation is relieved of the hardship, length, and severity of the standing.

His exalted words ﴿And say: My Lord, cause me to enter with a sound entry and cause me to exit with a sound exit﴾: this is another glad tiding that God the Exalted permitted His Messenger to migrate of his own accord, not by his people expelling him against his will. He said to him: say in your supplication, "My Lord, cause me to enter Medina, the abode of my migration, ﴿with a sound entry﴾, such that I see nothing disagreeable in it, and cause me to exit from Mecca on the day You cause me to exit ﴿with a sound exit﴾, not turning my heart back toward it in longing and yearning."

﴿And grant me from Yourself a supporting authority﴾: i.e., and ask Him to make for you from Himself an authority that will support you against whoever seeks you with harm, plots against you with deceit and treachery, tries to prevent you from establishing your religion and calling to your Lord. His exalted words ﴿And say: The truth has come and falsehood has vanished﴾ are another glad tiding that God the Exalted will open Mecca to him, and he will enter it victorious and triumphant, breaking the idols around the Kaaba, which were three hundred and sixty idols! And he says: "the truth has come and falsehood has vanished," i.e., disbelief has departed and been effaced. ﴿Indeed, falsehood is ever vanishing﴾: it has no permanence and no stability when it confronts the truth and stands against it. It is possible that by "the truth" is meant the Qur'an, and by "falsehood" lies and fabrication; it is also possible that "the truth" is Islam and "falsehood" is disbelief and polytheism, and more generally: the truth is everything that is obedience to God the Mighty and Majestic, and falsehood is every obedience to Satan, including polytheism, wrongdoing, and all other sins.

His exalted words ﴿And We send down of the Qur'an that which is a healing and a mercy for the believers﴾: i.e., and We send down upon you, O Our Messenger Muhammad, from the Qur'an that which is a healing, by which one is cured of the sickness of ignorance, misguidance, doubt, and whisperings, and a mercy for the believers rather than the disbelievers, because the believers act upon it, and God the Exalted shows them mercy by their acting upon His Book. As for the disbelievers, there is no mercy for them in it, because they deny it and abandon acting upon what it contains. His words ﴿and it does not increase the wrongdoers except in loss﴾: i.e., the Qur'an does not increase the wrongdoers, namely the obstinate polytheists who persisted in falsehood out of stubbornness and arrogance, except in loss, because the increase in their disbelief, wrongdoing, and obstinacy comes from what is sent down of the Qur'an that they hear.

His exalted words ﴿And when We bestow favor upon man, he turns away and withdraws his side; and when harm touches him, he is ever despairing﴾: God the Exalted informs about the disbelieving human being, deprived of the light of faith and the guidance of Islam, that when We bestow upon him the blessing of deliverance from destruction, having been brought near to drowning, sickness, hunger, or the like, he turns away from the remembrance of God and His supplication, as he used to supplicate Him in times of hardship, and he withdraws his side, i.e., he goes far from Us and does not turn to Us with his heart, and he goes off in his vanity and pride. His words ﴿and when harm touches him, he is ever despairing﴾ mean in despair (qunūṭ). This is the disbeliever, darkened in soul because of his disbelief and disobedience; when harm touches him, whether hunger, sickness, or fear encompasses him, he is ever very despairing and utterly hopeless, because he has no faith in God, in His mercy, or in His power to save him and deliver him.

His exalted words ﴿Say: Each acts according to his own manner, but your Lord knows best who is best guided on the path﴾: i.e., say, O Our Messenger, to the polytheists: each of us and of you acts according to his own way and doctrine, in accordance with his state of guidance or error. And your Lord, the Exalted, knows best who among us and you is better guided on the path. He will recompense everyone according to his deeds and conduct. This is a decisive word, cutting off the dispute arising from each party claiming to be upon the truth, that its religion is more correct, its way more excellent, and its path more beneficial and profitable.

Guidance of the verses:

1- The obligation of establishing the prayer and the explanation of its appointed times.

2- Encouragement toward supererogatory acts, especially tahajjud, the "night supererogatory prayer."

3- Affirmation of the Great Intercession of the Prophet ﷺ.

4- The weakness of falsehood and its swift vanishing when the truth confronts it and stands against it.

5- The Qur'an is a healing for the diseases of hearts in general and a mercy for the believers in particular.

6- Explanation of the nature of the disbelieving person and the description of the weakness that accompanies him.

7- Teaching the Messenger ﷺ and the believers how to free themselves from empty argument and unproductive debate.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 17, verses 85–89:

Explanation of the words:

Yas'alunaka 'an al-ruh: that is, the polytheists ask you, through the mediation of the People of the Book, about the ruh (spirit) by which the body is alive.

Min amri rabbi: that is, of His affair and knowledge, which He has kept to Himself and which no one else knows.

La-nadhhabanna bi-alladhi awhayna ilayka: that is, the Qur'an. If We willed, We would surely erase it from the breasts and the codices.

Laka bihi 'alayna wakilan: one who would prevent that from Us and stand between Us and what We wish to do to you.

Illa rahmatan min rabbik: that is, but We kept it preserved for you out of mercy from your Lord, so We did not take it away.

Bi-mithli hadha al-Qur'an: in eloquence, rhetorical power, and its content of unseen matters, laws, and rulings.

Zahiran: that is, a helper and a supporter.

Sarrafna: We explained to people, for their benefit, an example of every kind of example, so that they might take heed, believe, and affirm God's oneness.

Fa-aba aktharu al-nas: that is, the people of Makkah, except to disbelieve (kufuran), meaning rejecting the truth and persisting obstinately against it.

Meaning of the verses:

He, exalted is He, says: "They ask you about the ruh" (Yas'alunaka 'an al-ruh). The polytheists had asked him about the ruh, about the People of the Cave, and about Dhul-Qarnayn, at the instigation of the Jews of Madinah. God informed him of this and taught him the reply to them, so He said: "Say: The ruh is of the affair of my Lord" (Qul al-ruhu min amri rabbi), and of His knowledge, which none knows except Him. "And you have been given of knowledge only a little," because their asking this and similar questions indicates their claim to knowledge. So He informed them that what they had been given of knowledge is only little beside the knowledge of God, exalted is He.

His saying, exalted is He: "And if We willed, We would surely take away that which We have revealed to you" (Wa la'in shi'na la-nadhhabanna bi-alladhi awhayna ilayka): this is a favour from God upon His Messenger, to whom the Qur'an was sent down as a healing and a mercy for the believers, in that He, exalted is He, is able to erase it from his breast and from his written text, so that not a single verse remains. Then the Messenger would find no one to act as his protector against God's doing that to him. But out of His mercy, exalted is He, He did not will that; rather He keeps it until near the establishment of the Hour, as a proof of God against His servants and a sign of the prophethood of Muhammad ﷺ and the truth of his message. This is not the first of God's bounties upon His Messenger; God's favour upon him is great. Let us mention a portion of it: the generality of his message, that he is the Seal of the Prophets, his ascent to the highest kingdom, his leadership of the prophets, the Great Intercession, and the praiseworthy station.

His saying, exalted is He: "Say: If mankind and the jinn gathered together to produce the like of this Qur'an, they would not produce its like, even if some of them were helpers to others" (Qul la'in ijtama'at al-insu wal-jinnu 'ala an ya'tu bi-mithli hadha al-Qur'an la ya'tuna bi-mithlihi wa law kana ba'duhum li-ba'din zahiran). There is no doubt that what God taught His Messenger to say was caused by some people's claim that they were able to produce the like of this Qur'an, which is the sign of the truth of Muhammad's prophethood. Thereby the claim is refuted and their falsehood is defeated by the truth. So God commanded His Messenger to answer this false assertion by saying: "Say, O Our Messenger, to these claimants that they can produce the like of this Qur'an: if mankind and the jinn gathered together, cooperating and supporting one another in producing the like of this Qur'an, they would not produce its like, because it is the revelation of God and His Book, and His proof upon His creation."

And it is sufficient. How then could mankind and the jinn produce its like?!

His saying: "And We have certainly diversified for the people in this Qur'an" (Wa laqad sarrafna lil-nasi fi hadha al-Qur'an): that is, We have explained for the people an example of every kind of example, for the guidance and reform of people, so that perhaps they would remember and be admonished, believe, and affirm God's oneness. "But most of the people refused except disbelief" (Fa-aba aktharu al-nasi illa kufuran): that is, denial of the truth and rejection of the Qur'an and its calling it a lie, and of what it contains of truth, guidance, and light, because the divine decree had already preceded that Hell would be filled with the misguided and all of Iblis's hosts together.

Lessons from the verses:

1- The knowledge of the ruh is among the things God, exalted is He, has kept to Himself.

2- The knowledge of people, compared to God's knowledge, is no more than what a bird takes with its beak from the water of the ocean.

3- The preservation of the Qur'an in breasts and in written form until near the Hour.

4- The inability of mankind and the jinn to produce a Qur'an like the Noble Qur'an.

5- Because of what has preceded in God's knowledge regarding the wretchedness of people, you will find most of them do not believe.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 17, verses 85–89:

Explanation of the words:

Yas'alunaka 'an al-ruh: that is, the polytheists ask you, through the mediation of the People of the Book, about the ruh (spirit) by which the body is alive.

Min amri rabbi: that is, of His affair and knowledge, which He has kept to Himself and which no one else knows.

La-nadhhabanna bi-alladhi awhayna ilayka: that is, the Qur'an. If We willed, We would surely erase it from the breasts and the codices.

Laka bihi 'alayna wakilan: one who would prevent that from Us and stand between Us and what We wish to do to you.

Illa rahmatan min rabbik: that is, but We kept it preserved for you out of mercy from your Lord, so We did not take it away.

Bi-mithli hadha al-Qur'an: in eloquence, rhetorical power, and its content of unseen matters, laws, and rulings.

Zahiran: that is, a helper and a supporter.

Sarrafna: We explained to people, for their benefit, an example of every kind of example, so that they might take heed, believe, and affirm God's oneness.

Fa-aba aktharu al-nas: that is, the people of Makkah, except to disbelieve (kufuran), meaning rejecting the truth and persisting obstinately against it.

Meaning of the verses:

He, exalted is He, says: "They ask you about the ruh" (Yas'alunaka 'an al-ruh). The polytheists had asked him about the ruh, about the People of the Cave, and about Dhul-Qarnayn, at the instigation of the Jews of Madinah. God informed him of this and taught him the reply to them, so He said: "Say: The ruh is of the affair of my Lord" (Qul al-ruhu min amri rabbi), and of His knowledge, which none knows except Him. "And you have been given of knowledge only a little," because their asking this and similar questions indicates their claim to knowledge. So He informed them that what they had been given of knowledge is only little beside the knowledge of God, exalted is He.

His saying, exalted is He: "And if We willed, We would surely take away that which We have revealed to you" (Wa la'in shi'na la-nadhhabanna bi-alladhi awhayna ilayka): this is a favour from God upon His Messenger, to whom the Qur'an was sent down as a healing and a mercy for the believers, in that He, exalted is He, is able to erase it from his breast and from his written text, so that not a single verse remains. Then the Messenger would find no one to act as his protector against God's doing that to him. But out of His mercy, exalted is He, He did not will that; rather He keeps it until near the establishment of the Hour, as a proof of God against His servants and a sign of the prophethood of Muhammad ﷺ and the truth of his message. This is not the first of God's bounties upon His Messenger; God's favour upon him is great. Let us mention a portion of it: the generality of his message, that he is the Seal of the Prophets, his ascent to the highest kingdom, his leadership of the prophets, the Great Intercession, and the praiseworthy station.

2- The knowledge of people, compared to God's knowledge, is no more than what a bird takes with its beak from the water of the ocean.

3- The preservation of the Qur'an in breasts and in written form until near the Hour.

4- The inability of mankind and the jinn to produce a Qur'an like the Noble Qur'an.

5- Because of what has preceded in God's knowledge regarding the wretchedness of people, you will find most of them do not believe.

**Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 17, verses 90–95:**

**Explanation of the words:**

*Yanbu'an* (ينبوعاً): a spring whose water never runs dry, so it flows continuously.

*Jannah* (جنة): an orchard with many trees.

*Kisafan* (كسفاً): pieces, the plural of *kisfah*, like *qit'ah* (piece).

*Qabilan* (قبيلا): facing us, so that we see them directly.

*Min zukhruf* (من زخرف): of gold.

*Tarqa* (ترقى): you ascend into the sky.

*Mutma'innin* (مطمئنين): dwelling on the earth, not leaving it.

**The meaning of the verses:**

The noble context continues with the call to monotheism (tawhid), prophethood, and resurrection, and the affirmation of these. Almighty God says, reporting their words to the Messenger of Allah when they were disputing his prophethood: They said: ﴿We will not believe you﴾, meaning, we will not follow you in what you call to of monotheism, of your prophethood, and of resurrection and recompense for us, ﴿until you cause a spring to gush forth for us from the earth﴾, meaning a spring whose water flows on the surface of the earth without ceasing. ﴿Or you have a garden﴾, meaning an orchard of palms and grapes, ﴿and cause rivers to gush forth within it﴾, meaning in the midst of the trees, gushing forth abundantly. ﴿Or you cause the sky to fall upon us in pieces, as you claim﴾, meaning in fragments. ﴿Or you bring Allah and the angels before us﴾, meaning face to face, that we may see them directly. ﴿Or you have a house of gold﴾, meaning of gold, in which you dwell among us. ﴿Or you ascend into the sky﴾, meaning you climb up into the heaven by a ladder with rungs. ﴿And we will not believe in your ascent﴾ even if you ascend, ﴿until you bring down to us a book﴾ from Allah ﴿that we may read it﴾, commanding us in it to believe in you and follow you! These are six demands, each of which they regarded as a sign: whenever they witness it, they claim that they will believe, while Allah knows that they will not believe. Therefore He did not respond to them, and said to His Messenger: Say, O Muhammad, to them, ﴿Glory be to my Lord!﴾, marveling at their demands, ﴿Am I anything but a human messenger?﴾! Meaning: am I other than a human messenger? Otherwise, how could what they have requested be asked of me? What you demand is not within the power of a commanded servant like me. It lies only with a mighty, capable Lord, who says to a thing, "Be," and it is! I have not claimed lordship; I always declare that I am a servant of Allah and His messenger to you, to convey to you His message, that you worship Him alone, do not associate anything with Him, believe in the Last Resurrection, and act for it with obedience and abstention from sins.

And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And nothing prevented the people from believing when guidance came to them except that they said: Has Allah sent a human as a messenger?﴾ Meaning: nothing prevented the people of Makkah from believing when guidance came to them through their messenger, ﴿except that they said﴾, meaning, except their statement, ﴿Has Allah sent a human as a messenger?﴾, denying that Allah should send a messenger from among humans!

And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Say: Had there been in the earth angels walking securely, We would have sent down to them from the sky an angel as a messenger﴾. Meaning: say, O Our Messenger, to these deniers who marvel at this, that the messenger should be human: say to them, "If there were in the earth angels walking securely, dwelling on the earth and not leaving it, We would have sent down to them from the sky an angel as a messenger, guiding them by Our command and teaching them what is required of them by Our leave, because they would understand him, owing to the bond of kind and the mutual understanding that would be achieved between them." Therefore We have sent to you a messenger of your own kind, whom you understand, who is able to make you understand and to explain to you. So how, then, do you deny that humans may be messengers, when this is a matter that cannot be avoided?

**Guidance from the verses:**

1. Affirmation of the prophethood of the Messenger ﷺ.
2. Explanation of the extreme obstinacy of the polytheists of Quraysh, their rigidity, and their factionalism in the face of the call to monotheism.
3. Explanation of the folly of the polytheists' minds in accepting divinity in a stone while denying messengerhood to humans!
4. Affirmation that, according to Allah's sunnah, understanding is achieved only between beings of the same kind; when kinds differ, there is no mutual understanding, unless Allah wills it, so a human does not truly communicate with an animal or a jinn.

4. Affirmation that, according to Allah's sunnah, understanding is achieved only between beings of the same kind; when kinds differ, there is no mutual understanding, unless Allah wills it, so a human does not truly communicate with an animal or a jinn.

**Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 17, verses 90–95:**

**Explanation of the words:**

*Yanbu'an* (ينبوعاً): a spring whose water never runs dry, so it flows continuously.

*Jannah* (جنة): an orchard with many trees.

*Kisafan* (كسفاً): pieces, the plural of *kisfah*, like *qit'ah* (piece).

*Qabilan* (قبيلا): facing us, so that we see them directly.

*Min zukhruf* (من زخرف): of gold.

*Tarqa* (ترقى): you ascend into the sky.

*Mutma'innin* (مطمئنين): dwelling on the earth, not leaving it.

**The meaning of the verses:**

The noble context continues with the call to monotheism (tawhid), prophethood, and resurrection, and the affirmation of these. Almighty God says, reporting their words to the Messenger of Allah when they were disputing his prophethood: They said: ﴿We will not believe you﴾, meaning, we will not follow you in what you call to of monotheism, of your prophethood, and of resurrection and recompense for us, ﴿until you cause a spring to gush forth for us from the earth﴾, meaning a spring whose water flows on the surface of the earth without ceasing. ﴿Or you have a garden﴾, meaning an orchard of palms and grapes, ﴿and cause rivers to gush forth within it﴾, meaning in the midst of the trees, gushing forth abundantly. ﴿Or you cause the sky to fall upon us in pieces, as you claim﴾, meaning in fragments. ﴿Or you bring Allah and the angels before us﴾, meaning face to face, that we may see them directly. ﴿Or you have a house of gold﴾, meaning of gold, in which you dwell among us. ﴿Or you ascend into the sky﴾, meaning you climb up into the heaven by a ladder with rungs. ﴿And we will not believe in your ascent﴾ even if you ascend, ﴿until you bring down to us a book﴾ from Allah ﴿that we may read it﴾, commanding us in it to believe in you and follow you! These are six demands, each of which they regarded as a sign: whenever they witness it, they claim that they will believe, while Allah knows that they will not believe. Therefore He did not respond to them, and said to His Messenger: Say, O Muhammad, to them, ﴿Glory be to my Lord!﴾, marveling at their demands, ﴿Am I anything but a human messenger?﴾! Meaning: am I other than a human messenger? Otherwise, how could what they have requested be asked of me? What you demand is not within the power of a commanded servant like me. It lies only with a mighty, capable Lord, who says to a thing, "Be," and it is! I have not claimed lordship; I always declare that I am a servant of Allah and His messenger to you, to convey to you His message, that you worship Him alone, do not associate anything with Him, believe in the Last Resurrection, and act for it with obedience and abstention from sins.

And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And nothing prevented the people from believing when guidance came to them except that they said: Has Allah sent a human as a messenger?﴾ Meaning: nothing prevented the people of Makkah from believing when guidance came to them through their messenger, ﴿except that they said﴾, meaning, except their statement, ﴿Has Allah sent a human as a messenger?﴾, denying that Allah should send a messenger from among humans!

And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Say: Had there been in the earth angels walking securely, We would have sent down to them from the sky an angel as a messenger﴾. Meaning: say, O Our Messenger, to these deniers who marvel at this, that the messenger should be human: say to them, "If there were in the earth angels walking securely, dwelling on the earth and not leaving it, We would have sent down to them from the sky an angel as a messenger, guiding them by Our command and teaching them what is required of them by Our leave, because they would understand him, owing to the bond of kind and the mutual understanding that would be achieved between them." Therefore We have sent to you a messenger of your own kind, whom you understand, who is able to make you understand and to explain to you. So how, then, do you deny that humans may be messengers, when this is a matter that cannot be avoided?

**Guidance from the verses:**

1. Affirmation of the prophethood of the Messenger ﷺ.
2. Explanation of the extreme obstinacy of the polytheists of Quraysh, their rigidity, and their factionalism in the face of the call to monotheism.
3. Explanation of the folly of the polytheists' minds in accepting divinity in a stone while denying messengerhood to humans!
4. Affirmation that, according to Allah's sunnah, understanding is achieved only between beings of the same kind; when kinds differ, there is no mutual understanding, unless Allah wills it, so a human does not truly communicate with an animal or a jinn.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 17, verses 96–99:

Explanation of the words:

Shahidan (a witness): that I am the Messenger of God to you, that I have conveyed (the message) to you, and that you disbelieved and obstinately opposed.

Fa-lan tajida lahum awliya' (then you will not find for them protectors): i.e., who would guide them.

Ala wujuhihim (on their faces): i.e., they walk upon their faces.

Umyan wa-bukman wa-summan (blind, dumb and deaf): they do not see, do not speak, and do not hear.

Kullama khabat (whenever it dies down): i.e., whenever its flame subsides, We increase them in blaze (sa'ir), i.e., in flaring and blazing.

Wa-qalu (and they said): i.e., denying the Resurrection.

Mithlahum (their likes): i.e., people like them.

Ajalan (a term): a specified time.

Meaning of the verses:

The context continues to establish the Muhammadan prophethood. God says to His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ): Say to those deniers, who find it strange that a Messenger should be a human being, "﴿Sufficient is God as a witness between me and you﴾" that I am His Messenger, while you deny this against me.

He, may He be exalted, was and still is "﴿Aware of His servants, Seeing﴾", i.e., having complete knowledge of them and seeing their conditions. He knows the righteous from the wrongdoers, and the truthful from the liar, and He will recompense each according to His justice and mercy.

His saying, may He be exalted: "﴿Whomever God guides is the one who is guided﴾" informs that guidance is in the hand of God, the Exalted. Whomever God guides is truly guided. "﴿And whomever He leaves astray, you will not find for them protectors besides Him﴾", i.e., who could guide them in any way. In this statement there is consolation for the Messenger and solace concerning his people, who persist in denial and rejection of his message.

His saying: "﴿And We will gather them on the Day of Resurrection﴾", i.e., those deniers who went astray, who died in their misguidance and denial without repenting, We will gather them on the Day of Resurrection, walking upon their faces, while blind and not seeing, dumb and not speaking, deaf and not hearing. His saying, may He be exalted: "﴿Their refuge is Hell﴾", i.e., the place of their abode on that day is Hell, described as "﴿whenever its flame subsides﴾", i.e., whenever its blaze dies down for them, God increases them in blaze (sa'ir), i.e., in flaring and blazing. His saying, may He be exalted: "﴿That is their recompense﴾", i.e., that mentioned punishment is their recompense because they "disbelieved in God's signs", i.e., because of their disbelief in God's signs. Their saying, denying and deeming the Final Resurrection far-fetched: "﴿When we have become bones and crumbled remains, shall we truly be resurrected in a new creation?﴾", i.e., dust. God, may He be exalted, responded to their deeming the second life far-fetched, saying: "﴿Have they not seen﴾", i.e., do they deny the Final Resurrection? Have they not seen with the eyes of their hearts "﴿that God, who created the heavens and the earth, is able to create the likes of them﴾"?? Indeed, He is able, if only they knew!

His saying, may He be exalted: "﴿And He has appointed for them a term﴾", i.e., a specified, determined time for their destruction and punishment, "﴿about which there is no doubt﴾", and they are certainly going toward it. His saying: "﴿But the wrongdoers refused except disbelief﴾", i.e., despite this clarification and rational argument, the wrongdoers refused except denial and ingratitude, so that the word of punishment would be realized against them, and they would taste it, and we seek refuge in God, the Exalted.

Guidance from the verses:

1. The greatness of God's testimony and the obligation to be content with it.

2. Guidance and misguidance are in God's hand, so one must seek guidance from Him and seek refuge in Him from misguidance.

3. The dreadfulness of the punishment of the Day of Resurrection, when the wrongdoers are gathered walking upon their faces like serpents, deaf, dumb and blind, and we seek refuge in God, the Exalted, from the condition of the people of the Fire.

4. Hell is the recompense for disbelief in God's signs and for denying the Resurrection and the Requital on the Day of Judgment.

5. The proof of the Resurrection is rational as it is transmitted: the One Able to initiate is rationally able to restore, indeed restoration is, rationally, easier than initiating creation from nothing.
