Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 17, verses 100–104:

Explanation of the words:

"Khaza'in rahmati rabbi" (the treasuries of my Lord's mercy): that is, of rain and provisions.

"La-amsaktum" (you would have withheld): that is, you would have refrained from spending.

"Khashyata al-infaq" (for fear of spending): fear of exhaustion.

"Qatura" (niggardly): that is, one who is much given to stinginess, meaning miserliness and withholding of wealth.

"Tis'a ayatin bayyinat" (nine clear signs): that is, clear miracles, which are clear and evident, namely the hand, the staff, the effacement (of wealth), and so on.

"Mashura" (bewitched): that is, one whose mind has been overpowered, deluded.

"Ma anzala ha'ula'" (these have not been sent down): that is, these nine signs.

"Mathbura" (doomed): destroyed by your turning away from truth and good.

"Fa-arada an yastafizzahum" (so he resolved to drive them out): that is, to make them unsettled and expel them from the land of Egypt.

"Uskunu al-ard" (dwell in the land): that is, the land of Jerusalem and the Levant.

"Al-akhira" (the Hereafter): that is, the Hour.

"Lafifa" (gathered together): that is, mixed together from various living beings and tribes.

Meaning of the verses:

The Exalted says to His Messenger ﷺ: Say, O Muhammad, to those who demand that Mount Safa be turned into gold, and that the area around Mecca be turned into gardens of palm trees and grapevines through which rivers flow: Say to them, even if you possessed the treasuries of my Lord's mercy, of wealth and provisions, you would have withheld them, refusing to spend, for fear of their running out, since this is your nature, which is stinginess. ﴿And man has ever been niggardly﴾ before his guidance and faith, ﴿niggardly﴾, that is, excessively grudging out of miserliness and a soul's inner avarice that clings to him until he treats this avarice with the beneficial remedy that God the Exalted has prescribed, whose explanation came in Surat al-Ma'arij of this Noble Book.

And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And We certainly gave Moses nine clear signs﴾, that is, We gave Moses son of Imran, the prophet of the Children of Israel, nine signs, and they are: the hand, the staff, the blood, the splitting of the sea, the effacement of the wealth of Pharaoh's family, the flood, the locusts, the lice, and the frogs. Did Pharaoh's family believe in them? No. Therefore, if We had given you what your polytheist people demanded of the six signs they proposed, which were mentioned earlier in this noble context, they would not have believed in them, and hence there is no benefit in giving them to you.

And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿So ask the Children of Israel﴾, that is, ask, O our Prophet, the scholars of the Children of Israel, such as Abdullah ibn Salam and others, when Moses came to them, demanding from Pharaoh that he send them with him so that he might bring them out to the land of Jerusalem, and showed Pharaoh the signs that indicate the truthfulness of his prophethood and message, and the rightness of what he demanded. Pharaoh said to him: ﴿Indeed, I think you, O Moses, are bewitched﴾, that is, a sorcerer, for your displaying these extraordinary things you displayed, and "bewitched" means deluded, overpowered in your mind, so that you say what you say that no sensible person would say. Moses replied to him with what God the Exalted reported in His saying: ﴿You have certainly known﴾, that is, Pharaoh, that none sent down these clear signs except the Lord of the heavens, that is, their Creator, their Owner, and their Manager, ﴿as eyes-opening proofs﴾, that is, clear, luminous, guiding signs for whoever seeks guidance, but you were blinded to them while you knew their truth. ﴿And indeed, I think you, O Pharaoh, are doomed!﴾ That is, for this reason I think you, O Pharaoh, are cursed, removed far from God's mercy, destroyed and lost. When Pharaoh was overwhelmed by the proofs and clear evidence, he resorted to force, ﴿so he intended to drive them out from the land﴾, that is, to make them unsettled and expel them from the land of Egypt by mass killing to eradicate them, or by banishment, expulsion, and dispersal. The Lord the Exalted dealt with him in the opposite of what he intended, and God drowned him and his soldiers, all of them, which is the meaning of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Then We drowned him and those with him﴾, that is, of the soldiers, ﴿all together﴾. And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And We said after him﴾, that is, after the destruction of Pharaoh and his soldiers, to the Children of Israel through the tongue of Moses, peace be upon him: ﴿Dwell in the land﴾, that is, the land of Jerusalem and the Levant, until the end of your terms by death.

﴿So when the promise of the Hereafter comes﴾, that is, the Day of Resurrection, We will resurrect you alive as We resurrect others, ﴿We will bring you gathered together﴾, that is, mixed together from living beings, tribes, and various races, with no advantage of one over another, barefoot and naked, for the judgment to be decided, then the reckoning and recompense.

Guidance of the verses:

Among the guidance of these verses:

1- Stinginess is part of human nature, unless a person treats it with faith and piety, and God protects him from it.

2- Signs alone are not sufficient to guide a person; rather, divine success is necessary.

3- Manifestations of God the Exalted's power, His victory for His allies, and His subduing of His enemies.

4- An explanation of how people will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection, mixed together, a mingled crowd from various tribes and races.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 17, verses 105–109:

Explanation of the words:

﴿Wa-bil-haqqi anzalnahu﴾: That is, the Qur'an.

﴿Wa-bil-haqqi nazal﴾: That is, it descended with the clarification of the truth in worship, belief, reports, admonitions, wisdom and rulings.

﴿Wa-Qur'anan faraqnahu﴾: That We sent it down in parts over the course of twenty-three years, for a wisdom that required this.

﴿Ala mukth﴾: That is, at a measured and deliberate pace, so that the listener may understand it.

﴿Wa-nazzalnahu tanzilan﴾: That is, little by little, according to the interests of the community, so that it may be made complete through it and so that it may be made happy by it.

﴿Utul-'ilma min qablihi﴾: That is, the believers among the People of the Book, from the Jews and the Christians, such as 'Abdullah ibn Salam and Salman al-Farisi.

﴿Lil-adhqani sujjadan﴾: That is, prostrating upon their faces. Whoever prostrates upon his face has fallen upon his chin in prostration.

﴿In kana wa'du rabbina lamaf'ulan﴾: Fulfilled, realized. He has sent the unlettered Prophet about whom His books gave good tidings, and He has sent down His Book upon him.

The meaning of the verses:

He, the Exalted, says: ﴿And with the truth We have sent it down﴾, that is, this Book which the deniers have rejected and which the polytheists have denied, We sent it down with the established truth, since there is no doubt that it is the Book of God and His revelation to His Messenger. ﴿And with the truth it has descended﴾, so everything that it contains, calls to, and commands is truth. What it reports of beliefs, legislation, reports, promises and warnings is all established truth, with no dispute in it and no doubt about it. As for His statement, the Exalted: ﴿And We have not sent you except as a bringer of good tidings and a warner﴾, that is, We did not send you to create guidance in the hearts of Our servants, nor to compel them by the force of authority to believe in Us and to affirm Our oneness; rather We sent you for calling and conveying. ﴿A bringer of good tidings﴾ to whoever obeys Us, with Paradise, and ﴿a warner﴾ to whoever disobeys Us, frightening him with the Fire. In this is an affirmation of his mission and prophethood (ﷺ). As for His statement, the Exalted: ﴿And a Qur'an which We have divided that you may recite it to the people over a measured pace﴾, that is, We sent down the Qur'an and divided it over the course of twenty-three years for a wisdom from Us that required this. And His statement ﴿that you may recite it to the people over a measured pace﴾, verse after verse, so that this is more conducive to the understanding of whoever hears and listens to it. As for His statement, the Exalted: ﴿And We have sent it down in gradual revelation﴾, that is, little by little according to the interests of the servants and what their spiritual and human upbringing requires, so that they may be perfected by it in intellect, morals and spirit, and be made happy by it in both abodes. As for His statement: ﴿Say: Believe in it or do not believe﴾, that is, say, O Our Messenger, to the deniers of the Qur'anic revelation from your people: believe in it or do not believe; for your belief in it is like its absence and does not change its reality in any way. Others will believe in it and be made happy by it if you do not believe in it. Behold, those who were given knowledge before it, from the scholars of the two People of the Book, the Jews and the Christians, have already believed in it, meaning the likes of 'Abdullah ibn Salam, Salman al-Farisi, and al-Najashi Ashama al-Habashi. Indeed they, ﴿when it is recited to them﴾, that is, when it is read to them, ﴿they fall down upon their chins prostrating﴾, that is, they fall prostrating upon their chins and faces, and they say during their prostration: ﴿Glory be to our Lord﴾, that is, exalted is He above breaking His promise, since He promised that He would send a Prophet at the end of time and send down upon him a Qur'an. ﴿Indeed the promise of our Lord has been fulfilled﴾, as an acknowledgment from them of the Muhammadan prophethood and the Great Qur'an; that is, it has been carried out, since He promised to send the Seal of the Prophets and to send down the Book upon him, and He fulfilled what He promised. Thus the promise of our Lord is always fulfilled and never fails. As for His statement: ﴿And they fall down upon their chins weeping﴾, that is, when they hear the Qur'an they do not merely prostrate, but they fall down weeping, and the hearing and recitation of the Qur'an increase them in humility in their hearts and tranquility in their limbs, because it is the truth they heard from their Lord.

Guidance of the verses:

Among the guidance of these verses:

1- The Qur'an is the truth from God, and everything it was sent down with is truth.

2- Recommendation to recite the Qur'an measuredly, especially when reciting it to people to call them to God, the Exalted.

3- Affirmation that the Qur'an was sent down in parts over twenty-three years.

4- Affirmation of Muhammadan prophethood through the descent of the Qur'an and the belief of those among the People of the Book who believed in it.

5- Clarification of the reality of prostration, that it is placing the face upon the ground.

6- Legitimacy of prostration for the reciter or the listener, and its being a sunnah when reciting this verse, which is: ﴿And they fall down upon their chins weeping, and it increases them in humility﴾. So one falls prostrate, saying "Allahu Akbar" in lowering and in rising, glorifying, and supplicating in his prostration with whatever he wishes.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 17, verses 110–111:

Explanation of the words:

"Call upon Allah or call upon the Most Gracious (ar-Rahman)": that is, name Him by either of them and call upon Him by each one of them, Allah or ar-Rahman.

"Whichever you call": that is, if you call upon Him by either of them, it is good, because to Him belong the Most Beautiful Names (al-asma' al-husna), and these two are among them.

"And do not recite your prayer aloud": that is, do not recite your Qur'an in the prayer loudly, out of dislike that the polytheists should hear it and revile you, revile the Qur'an, and revile the One who sent it down.

"Nor recite it in a low voice": that is, do not recite it so quietly that your companions who pray behind you cannot benefit from your recitation in the prayer.

"And seek a way between those": that is, seek a middle path between secrecy and loudness.

"He has not taken a son": as the disbelievers say.

"Nor has He any partner": as the polytheists say.

"Nor has He any ally out of weakness": that is, He has no protector who supports Him out of need, since He is the Mighty, the Compelling, the Owner of the Kingdom, Possessor of Majesty and Honour.

"And magnify Him with complete magnification": that is, exalt Him with complete exaltation above having a son, a partner, or an ally out of weakness.

The meaning of the verses:

The Prophet (ﷺ) used to say in his supplication, "O Allah! O Rahman! O Rahman, O Rahim!" The polytheists heard him, and they were searching for any doubt they could raise against him. When they heard him say "O Allah, O Rahman," they said: "Look at him, how he calls upon two gods and forbids us from that!" So Allah the Exalted sent down: ﴿Say: Call upon Allah or call upon the Most Gracious﴾, that is, say to them, O our Prophet, "Call upon Allah or call upon the Most Gracious; for Allah is the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful," ﴿Whichever you call upon, to Him belong the Most Beautiful Names﴾, that is, whichever of the two you call upon, Allah or the Most Gracious, He is Allah, Possessor of the Most Beautiful Names and the Sublime Attributes. And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And do not recite your prayer aloud, nor recite it in a low voice, but seek a way between those﴾, that is, a middle course between secrecy and loudness. This was because the polytheists, when they heard the Qur'an, would revile its reciter and the One who sent it down. So Allah the Exalted commanded His Messenger, and the believers who follow him, when they recite in their prayer, not to be loud, lest the polytheists hear their recitation, and not to be silent, lest those who pray behind them be deprived of hearing the Qur'an. So the Messenger of Allah was commanded to take a middle course between loudness and secrecy.

And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And say: Praise be to Allah, who has not taken a son, and has no partner in the dominion, and has no ally out of weakness, and magnify Him with full magnification﴾. That is, Allah the Exalted commanded the Messenger to praise Allah, who has not taken a son, as some Arabs claimed when they said, "The angels are the daughters of Allah!" and as the Jews claimed when they said, "Ezra is the son of Allah," and the Christians when they said, "Jesus is the son of Allah!" ﴿Nor has He any partner in the dominion﴾, as the polytheists of the Arabs said: "Here I am, O Allah, here I am; here I am, You have no partner, here I am, except a partner who is Yours, You own him and what he owns!"

﴿Nor has He any ally out of weakness﴾, as the Sabians and the Magians said: "Were it not for the allies of Allah, Allah would be humbled!"

﴿And magnify Him﴾: you, or exalt Him, O our Messenger, with exaltation above having any attribute of deficiency, need, or incapacity.

Guidance from the verses:

1- Allah has the Most Beautiful Names, and they are a hundred names except one. So Allah is called upon and addressed by any of them, and all of them are beautiful, as Allah says in Surah al-A'raf: ﴿And to Allah belong the Most Beautiful Names, so call upon Him by them﴾ [Verse: 180].

2- A clarification of what the polytheists of Makkah were upon, of hatred toward the Messenger, the Qur'an, and the believers.

3- The legitimacy of taking precaution for the religion just as one does for worldly affairs.

4- The obligation to praise Allah, extol Him, and declare Him free of every incapacity and deficiency.

5- This verse ﴿And say: Praise be to Allah, who has not taken a son, and has no partner in the dominion, and has no ally out of weakness﴾ is called the Verse of Honour (ayat al-'izz); this is what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) named it.

That is, Allah the Exalted commanded the Messenger to praise Allah, who has not taken a son, as some Arabs claimed when they said, "The angels are the daughters of Allah!" and as the Jews claimed when they said, "Ezra is the son of Allah," and the Christians when they said, "Jesus is the son of Allah!" ﴿Nor has He any partner in the dominion﴾, as the polytheists of the Arabs said: "Here I am, O Allah, here I am; here I am, You have no partner, here I am, except a partner who is Yours, You own him and what he owns!"

﴿Nor has He any ally out of weakness﴾, as the Sabians and the Magians said: "Were it not for the allies of Allah, Allah would be humbled!"

﴿And magnify Him﴾: you, or exalt Him, O our Messenger, with exaltation above having any attribute of deficiency, need, or incapacity.

Guidance from the verses:

1- Allah has the Most Beautiful Names, and they are a hundred names except one. So Allah is called upon and addressed by any of them, and all of them are beautiful, as Allah says in Surah al-A'raf: ﴿And to Allah belong the Most Beautiful Names, so call upon Him by them﴾ [Verse: 180].

2- A clarification of what the polytheists of Makkah were upon, of hatred toward the Messenger, the Qur'an, and the believers.

3- The legitimacy of taking precaution for the religion just as one does for worldly affairs.

4- The obligation to praise Allah, extol Him, and declare Him free of every incapacity and deficiency.

5- This verse ﴿And say: Praise be to Allah, who has not taken a son, and has no partner in the dominion, and has no ally out of weakness﴾ is called the Verse of Honour (ayat al-'izz); this is what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) named it.
